One source said the official Fifa party had attempted to portray their governance crisis as a private dispute between Infantino and Montagliani. The Canadian businessman has not commented since news of the proposed Fifa Forward Enterprise emerged, but has been widely touted in Europe as a possible contender to replace Infantino.

The pair met briefly and shook hands before the CFU meeting in an exchange captured by Infantino’s personal camera crew.

While Mexico, Grenada and St Kitts and Nevis have all broken with Concacaf and declared their support for Infantino, the majority of their 41 members are understood to back the alliance with Uefa advocated by Montagliani.

The Uefa/Concacaf pact extends beyond attempts to unseat Infantino, with the two confederations in talks about setting up a joint Nations League in 2028 that could develop further into a new global competition.

Sports.title: Meet the new Spurs, same as the old Spurs despite big summer spending | Billy Munday
Sports.content:
This was supposed to be New Spurs. Daniel Levy, such a magnet for fan apathy, has been sidelined. Roberto De Zerbi’s recruitment drive has won the transfer market. The stadium is still nice. But Spurs and ambition were always an awkward combination and all those cash-fuelled dreams were shattered within an hour of the new season. A few headed for the exits after Brentford’s third goal on 49 minutes. There were not many left by the time those in freakish purple made their way over to that corner of the Gtech at full time.

There was no escaping the irony that the best player on the splendid opening-day pitch was the only new face in Brentford’s starting XI. Mamadou Sangaré, signed for a club-record fee from Lens, made sure his Premier League debut was played at his pace – faster and more dynamic than any of Sandro Tonali, Lucas Bergvall or Conor Gallagher could deal with in midfield. The Mali international ran off Bergvall to set up Keane Lewis-Potter’s first and struck the shot that led to Michael Kayode’s third.

Sangaré is an example of what happens when a club gets its recruitment right. The 24-year-old is clearly a player on the up – and has the temperament to match his talent. His career has not been easy, moving to Europe and Red Bull Salzburg at 18 but spending his years in Austria on loans in the second tier and in Belgium. After a year at Lens that included Coupe de France glory and individual Ligue 1 accolades, Brentford paid what already looks like a bargain £41m. The standing ovation at his second-half withdrawal was the least he deserved.

On the other side, Tonali was the face of Tottenham’s troubles, the £100m marquee signing playing a game where the ball seemed to elude him, tease him from afar. De Zerbi has spoken this summer of how impressed he had been watching the midfielder play as a teenager for the Italian club he supports, Brescia. He looked considerably less impressed with the 26-year-old version after he skied a volley high over the crossbar on 40 minutes, completing a first half of misplaced passes and frustrated fouls, always one step behind the imperious Sangaré.

View image in fullscreen Mamadou Sangaré emphatically won the battle of the midfield summer signings against Sandro Tonali. Photograph: Gaspafotos/MB Media/Getty Images

De Zerbi is known for his boldness – and there was certainly something to be said for making Archie Gray the youngest captain in Tottenham’s history in the absence of the injured new club skipper, Micky van de Ven. You could forgive his predecessor, Cristian Romero, for feeling a touch smug in his new Madrid apartment. The edgy Marcos Senesi, such an unflappable figure amid the turnover in the Bournemouth defence last season, clearly spent too much time with his Argentina teammate Romero at the World Cup. His defensive partner, Jan Paul van Hecke, has not settled in either. Scotland’s captain, Andy Robertson, led out by the 20-year-old Gray here, must be asking what he has let himself in for.

So must Savinho and Omar Marmoush, pending arrivals that will take Spurs’ summer spending towards the dizzying heights of £400m – only Liverpool in 2025 have spent more in a single window out of any club, anywhere. Spurs had brought in six new players before a ball was kicked but still started the season with Richarlison leading the line. The contrast between his meek performance and that of his compatriot and opposite number Igor Thiago, combining power and poise, felt significant. The ease with which Brentford’s No 9 had it all afternoon was evident in his over-relaxed penalty that pinged back off the foot of a post at 3-0.

After establishing a two-goal lead through Lewis-Potter and Vitaly Janelt, Brentford were unfazed by Spurs’ introduction of their £85m signing Mateus Fernandes at the break and carried on where they left off. How high can they fly this season? Unlike many of their rivals, Keith Andrews’ side are without the burden of European football after missing out on the final day of last season. Second-half substitutes such as Jaidon Anthony and Callum Wilson are handy additions of firepower at a fraction of the cost in a market that is ballooning off the back of Spurs’ wild spending.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Tottenham started last season with a 3-0 win over Burnley and a 2-0 victory at Manchester City – points that promised a new beginning under Thomas Frank, who haunted them from his old manor here, but ultimately proved vital in their fight for survival under De Zerbi in May. Where does this result and performance leave the head coach? This will probably work out eventually – his vastly changed squad must be given time to gel. But what if this is New Spurs? A constant cycle of new lows and new ways of embarrassing themselves. After two 17th-place finishes in succession, would anyone blame them for taking that now?

Sports.title: Lincoln spirits soar despite defeat on second-tier return 65 years in the making
Sports.content:
There is optimism to be found in almost every corner of the footballing landscape at this time of the year, but on a sunny Saturday lunchtime in one of Britain’s most picturesque cities, you would do well to find anyone without a smile on their face.

Football may not necessarily be the first thing that springs to mind when you think of Lincoln. After all, Sincil Bank sits in the shadow of the imposing cathedral, high on the hill and a building that symbolically represents the importance of this area stretching back hundreds of years.

But the city’s sporting pride is writing its own slice of history. Yuri Gagarin had only just returned from space when Lincoln last hosted second-tier football, a 2-0 win over Leyton Orient in 1961. But after more than 65 years, the Imps are a Championship side again, having won League One last season with more than 100 points.

View image in fullscreen Lincoln won League One last season in style, finishing top by 12 points. Photograph: Harriet Massey/Getty Images

Sincil Bank housed the biggest attendance here, 10,545 for more than 40 years for their return to the second tier. While the majority left disappointed as Portsmouth inflicted a second consecutive defeat on the hosts to start the season, the mood did not feel too dampened given the extraordinary journey this club have enjoyed of late.

Most of Lincoln’s recent history has been in the footballing wilderness, but there is rapid change, both on and off the pitch. The Imps have spent £10m over the summer modernising the ground with a new fan village, big screen and upgrades to the stands that were all-but sold out.

There is change in the dugout, too, with Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw jointly taking over from Michael Skubala, but some things do not change. The air raid siren – a nod to the city’s military history – still sounds every time a Lincoln corner booms its way into the opposition area and the dedication to a traditional 4-4-2, which has seen them rise through the leagues, endures.

Whether it will need adapting over the course of this season remains to be seen, but for now, Lincoln are backing what has got them this far. The most important constant is the deep-rooted connection between supporters and team, which has helped fuel their progression. Togetherness is at the heart of everything.

Barely a soul left before the final whistle, even when Ebou Adams’s strike secured a first win of the season for Portsmouth in the 69th minute. Many supporters stayed behind in the new fan village to debrief the loss and they remain generally upbeat. Given how far they have come, it will take more than two defeats to steer this club off course.

Had Ben House scored when through on goal early on, this historic afternoon may have been one of celebration. But Portsmouth underlined the step up in quality shortly after, going 2-0 ahead with wonderful strikes from Ryan Kavuma-McQueen and Adrian Segecic.

View image in fullscreen Defeat by Portsmouth did not detract from a celebratory day for those associated with Lincoln. Photograph: Mark Kerton/Shutterstock

Reeco Hackett’s penalty before the break gave the Imps hope but Adams sealed the deal for Pompey.

“It’s been an amazing day for the club,” Shaw said. “The atmosphere was fantastic at the start of the game and it all aligned lovely until the goal.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“People have waited a long time to have a Championship football match here and I desperately hope we can have some good results here. But the ball moves around a bit quicker at this level, the quality increases so we’ve got to be a bit more alive to certain situations.”

To take this afternoon on face value would perhaps be overlooking the more important story. Lincoln represent a beacon of hope not just for themselves, but for much of the EFL; showing that aggressively spending beyond your means is not the only way to achieve success. If they can go from non-league to the Championship in 10 years, why can’t anyone?

View image in fullscreen Reeco Hackett became the first Lincoln player to score a second-tier goal at Sincil Bank since Joe Buick in April 1961. Photograph: Chris Vaughan/Getty Images

Perhaps money is not everything. Instead, success can be built on spirit, being greater than the sum of your parts and a bond between all involved. This club is still firmly in touch with what matters; the revamped Stacey West Stand bears the name of the two fans who died in the Bradford fire disaster of 1985, while the family zones were packed with the next generation of Lincoln fans keen for their first real glimpse of their new heroes.

This is not their first rodeo as underdogs, either. Lincoln weren’t supposed to win League Two in 2019. They certainly weren’t supposed to win League One with a mid-table budget last year, a division that included Cardiff, Luton and Bolton.

This time around, they are not expected to survive the Championship; they may not beat the odds this time, but with that spirit of togetherness behind them, they will give it a thoroughly good go.

Sports.title: José Mourinho marks Real Madrid return with late drama and touch of humility
Sports.content:
José Mourinho says he is calmer now so when the rest of the bench emptied, sprinting down the touchline to celebrate the 90th-minute goal that finally delivered victory on his first game in charge of Real Madrid in 4,380 days, he didn’t set off with them. Instead, he clenched his fists, got to his feet and walked down the touchline behind the subs, watching them head, shouting, towards Carlos Espí. As they piled on down in the corner, he pulled over his captain Fede Valverde for a word. Which might just have been: phew.

For all those stars; for all that Mourinho’s main task might just have been been to find a way to fit Kylian Mbappé, Vinícius Júnior and Jude Bellingham together; for all that he had introduced Yan Diomande, the most expensive player in the club’s history, it was a 21-year-old, unknown six months ago and unexpectedly signed from Levante, who got the goal that secured victory upon the coach’s second coming.

Espí, whose goals had rescued Levante from relegation last season and who is still living at Madrid’s Valdebebas training ground like his coach, the two of them sharing breakfast every morning, was signed for pretty much this: to be a different type of striker, an old-school No 9, with a presence in the area. And when a scrappy, broken-up move ended with Mbappé seeing the ball run away from him in the area, there he was to force it over the line. Perhaps even to pose a question: is his a profile they could do with and not just in reserve? This time, at least, it had worked.

View image in fullscreen Carlos Espí celebrates the late winner for Real Madrid. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

Mourinho’s first game since a 4-2 win over Osasuna in May 2013 began with the photographers abandoning their places behind the goal to surround him on the bench, no doubt what the attraction was; it ended with him hugging the Espanyol coach Manolo González, high-fiving the referee and ducking down the tunnel. In between time, reality was revealed, which he surely always imagined it would be: it is early, solutions are never immediate, and he had said that Espanyol were a good side. At times, they showed it too. Madrid had more chances, but Manolo’s team had largely succeeded in limiting the visitors.

On a night where Madrid exhibited some of the old flaws, there were doubts still – it is the first day after all – but they were at least allayed for a little while. There will be other days, sterner tests of this team; there will also be sterner tests of Mourinho’s temperament, of course.

When Madrid faced Benfica in the spring, Mourinho had described his time there as “three hard, intense, sometimes violent years”. But the thing about nostalgia is that as the bad slips into the distance, only the good remains. Mourinho said that he is “not the kind of man who misses anything”, someone who has “regrets”; plenty though had missed him, the president Florentino Pérez first among them. In his world view, managers are mostly a necessary evil; the Portuguese is virtually the only coach he had ever truly liked.

There are those who had longed for exactly that intensity, violence even: for a hard man to lead them, some kind of iron surgeon to fix them and go to war with their rivals, someone with the personality to impose. For all that by the end they really could not go on, at some level Pérez had always been drawn to Mourinho’s return. He clung to the idea that their success after his departure – six Champions League wins in 11 years – was down to him, that he had made it possible. He had shown the way.

Mourinho told a story on the eve of this game revealing that after every trophy Madrid won he would have got a call from Pérez. “I always said no, no, no, it was nothing to do with me,” he said, which was a neat way of saying it kind of was. This was not a confidence betrayed: Pérez had said much the same. It took the president 13 years to attend to his urge, but now Mourinho was back.

And, perhaps, why not? The last returnees had done rather well, while all the others had failed. There was a moment at the end of that story when Mourinho said the trophies belonged to Zinedine Zidane and Carlo Ancelotti, not him, and innocently checked that they were the only men to have won anything. The diagnosis of their ills, the challenge before them, required his surgery too. Like in 2010, Madrid had fallen behind Barcelona. They have not won a major title in two years, and that was about culture as well as football.

View image in fullscreen A first look of Yan Diomande in action for Real Madrid against Espanyol. Photograph: Quality Sport Images/Getty Images

It may not be as simple as effort but that is a start. “We have to try not to negotiate things that are non-negotiable,” Mourinho said. “Commitment can’t be missing.” Mourinho has the authority to change that, or so it goes. He would be afforded it, anyway. That at least is the theory. Habits had been changed, demands made. Sessions had improved, or the attitude towards them. Diomande had said he was ready to “die” for his coach, who insisted that was just a phrase, but he could not help but be pleased with that.

There were other reasons to be optimistic. Vinícius’s future had been resolved at last, no lingering doubts over status or resentment. The World Cup is out the way, no other priority on the horizon. Mourinho noted that Brazil, France and England had found a way to get the best out of Vinícius, Mbappe and Bellingham, but that getting the best of all three is different. “I don’t think they’re incompatible,” he insisted; last year it often looked like they were, Bellingham, admitting that they find themselves occupying the same spaces at times.

Here, they all started. Bellingham was at No 10, Vinícius tight to the touchline. “For me this is his [Jude’s] position: the connection with the forwards, he can score goals. He has to play close to the goal. Playing at 6 or 8 we’re losing his closeness to the goal,” said Mourinho.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Bellingham had an immediate impact, the first goal of this new era coming from a dead ball and after nine minutes. Vinícius was fouled, which was already looking like becoming a pattern – Alex Calatrava had already given him a kick in the back, prompting Mourinho to raise his arms – and from the left, Arda Guler delivered a superb cross. Bellingham leapt highest to head past Marko Dimitrovic.

View image in fullscreen Jude Bellingham celebrates after giving Real the lead. Photograph: David Ramos/Getty Images

This time, sitting on the left end of the bench, Mourinho barely flinched. He got up, put his hands in his pockets and walked along the touchline to the other end where the rest of his sizeable staff sat in the overspill in the stand beyond the other end. There, he shook hands with Sami Khedira, the in-house assistant Madrid have provided him, and Roberto Merella, the analyst.

And that, it was tempting to assume, was that. The gap between the teams looked insurmountable. Madrid were pressing high, Espanyol barely able to find a way out. Here was a glimpse, they might have hoped, of the future. Instead, the intensity dropped again and that was an invitation for Espanyol.

When Dean Huijsen needed attention for a cut, Madrid’s players came to Mourinho for instructions but the game started to slip from them a little. Espanyol took a step forward and soon had an equaliser. Thibaut Courtois saved from Riedel, Roberto Fernández unable to keep down the follow-up. Then a lovely move concluded with Tuy Dolan and Javi Hernández setting up Calatrava to score. Mourinho sat almost motionless.

Twice Mbappé escaped to force saves from Dimitrovic, one on each side of the area, but it was Espanyol who should have led at the break. Again, the ball was worked into position. From the right, Omar El Hilali provided a superb cross. Dolan couldn’t quite get to it, inside the six-yard box, and Fernández headed it straight at his own feet. Mbappé may wonder how he didn’t put Madrid into the lead just after the break. From Guler’s corner, Bellingham headed against the bar, via Dimitrovic’s hand, and the ball dropped to the Frenchman right by the post. Somehow, it went wide.

Valverde hit the post, Mbappé shot wide, but there was no way through. Mourinho turned to the men behind him – Cucurella, Diomande, Camavinga, Alexander-Arnold, Espí – until, at last, he saw them dash past him, given a reprieve on his return.

“I think we deserved to win, but Espanyol didn’t deserve to lose,” Mourinho said as he ended the night with a touch of humility.

Sports.title: Aston Villa upheaval is a risk but Emery can release v2.0 and reap rewards | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Last season was the greatest Aston Villa have enjoyed since they won the European Cup in 1982. They claimed their second European trophy by lifting the Europa League, but even without that would have secured Champions League qualification by finishing fourth in the Premier League.

Despite a miserable start during which they failed to win any of their first five league games, there was even a spell around Christmas when it looked as though Villa might be challengers for the title. The question after a season like that is always: where next?

The answer is probably less clear now than it was amid the delirium of Istanbul in May. A reasonable consideration, even a couple of weeks ago, would have been: was that a one-off high, the limit of the club’s ambitions, or was there more? The danger for any team, but particularly one relatively unfamiliar with success, is to rest on its laurels, to be too loyal to those who have brought the long-awaited silverware.

It’s an understandable enough impulse: any transfer comes with a risk, so why make changes when what was there before worked? Why offload players to whom there is a sense of gratitude? Villa have not rested on their laurels.

Three major players – Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Ezri Konsa – have left, Emí Martínez seems likely to join them and Ollie Watkins might go as well. This is not a fire sale. Nor is it a club cashing in while it still can. But it probably wasn’t quite planned this way either. The exodus is a combination of accepting that certain players are ready to fly the nest and trying to make as much money from them as possible for a rejuvenation of the squad. The danger is that too much is being changed too quickly.

Those changes have not just been among the playing staff. Two physios and the head of the medical team went to Arsenal. Jaime Arias Galán, a technical assistant, has left. The individual development coach, Rodri, went to Como. Most significantly, Unai Emery’s assistant, Pako Ayestarán, departed, while the set-piece coach, Austin MacPhee, went to Chelsea. There are always changes among backroom staff and the impact is hard for outsiders to assess but, still, the departures add to the sense of flux and uncertainty.

There is logic in the changes to playing personnel, though. Rogers is 24 and had been at the club for two and a half seasons. He scored 14 goals in all competitions in each of the past two seasons, many of them spectacular. He squeezed in the third goal in the Europa League final and will be remembered with great affection by Villa fans but he wanted to go for the better salary and perceived better opportunities (a risk, frankly) at Chelsea.

View image in fullscreen Johan Manzambi was a flowing sight for Switzerland at the World Cup this summer. Photograph: Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images

Once a player’s mind is set on leaving, there is rarely much point in standing in their way. An Alexander Isak at Newcastle situation helps nobody. Far better to accept the cash and reinvest it. For a player who cost £15m, a fee of £117m, less the 20% owed to Middlesbrough, represents excellent business.

Konsa is 28 but had two years left on his contract. A fee of £51m feels reasonable. Tielemans went after Manchester United triggered his £35m release clause. There was nothing Villa could have done but, given the Belgian is 29, they can at least console themselves that they’re selling a player they picked up on a free in summer 2023 for a reasonable price before any decline has begun. While no club enjoys losing high-class players, trading is a necessary part of squad development – and there is reason to be excited about Villa’s recruitment.

Johan Manzambi is a hugely gifted young attacking midfielder, Zion Suzuki is recognised as one of the most promising young goalkeepers in the world, João Gomes has already shown signs of the tenacity he can bring to the midfield and Matteo Ruggeri probably represents an upgrade on Lucas Digne at left-back. Alejandro Garnacho is a loan signing with potential. The Argentinian winger clearly has talent; the issue is releasing it consistently. Aaron Wan-Bissaka, reliable cover at right-back, has joined from relegated West Ham.

And all that with a net surplus of £160m, plus whatever they may get for Watkins should he leave. More signings will arrive. There is need of a defender to replace Konsa. Chelsea’s Nicolas Jackson represents an obvious option to replace Watkins, given his capacity to exploit the space behind opposing defensive lines. The thought of him and Manzambi linking with Brian Madjo, the 17-year-old centre-forward who made such an impression in the Uefa Super Cup defeat by Paris Saint-Germain, is undeniably enticing.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Another central midfielder looks essential, particularly after Amadou Onana tore his anterior cruciate ligament at the World Cup. There will probably be at least one and possible two more creative players, one to operate centrally and one in the left.

View image in fullscreen Villa’s teenage forward Brian Madjo gave Paris Saint-German a torrid time in this month’s Super Cup. Photograph: Joao Bravo/Sports Press Photo/Shutterstock

That means potentially seven or eight major arrivals over the summer, and that is a lot. It hasn’t always been easy for new signings to adapt themselves to Emery’s methods. The Spaniard has insisted there are “six or seven contenders” who are better equipped than Villa this season.

Managers habitually try to play down expectation and, given the changes, it’s understandable Emery should take that stance. It may even be accurate. But it’s also true that a lot of sides have undergone a lot of change this season – and Villa at least have retained the same manager.

It may even be that this is a necessary stage of development, of rejuvenation and of the accumulation of capital before a renewed assault on the heights. Certainly the shift from Profitability and Sustainability Rules to squad cost ratio should suit Villa. But in an ideal world, all three of Rogers, Konsa and Tielemans would not have gone in the same summer; to undergo this much change at once is an enormous risk.

It is, though, risk with a potential upside, whereas sitting back and relishing the memory of last season would have led inevitably to decline. One phase is ending, a new one beginning and, while it might go wrong, Emery 2.0 may, in time, be even better for Villa than the first version.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca searches for ‘new Rodri’ and expects Manchester City reaction
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca has brushed off the loss of Rodri to Barcelona for £65m by stating Manchester City will search for the “new Rodri” in the same way Sergio Agüero was replaced by Erling Haaland.

Rodri’s departure is a sizable blow to the club’s new manager as he embarks on a first season in charge. Yet the Italian is not fazed by the absence of a player considered one of the world’s best No 6s.

“How do we solve that problem? We try to find the new Rodri, it is what it is. [Before] Rodri arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. He joined the club, then he achieved many important things.

“Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri. I was thinking on Thursday night, when David Silva was here, everyone was worried and Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio [Agüero] was here, everyone was worried [when he was going to leave] and Erling [Haaland] arrived. Fernandinho? Rodri arrived. It is just about this. When they leave, you need to be good at recruiting the next one.

“They are all similar, David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Erling – it is normal, it is change, it is not a problem, go again and try to do the right things.”

Rodri had expressed his desire to leave City and Maresca said – as did his predecessor, Pep Guardiola – he would not stand in the way of any player who wishes to leave. “He can go, absolutely. If he is not happy, he is not going to perform in the right way,” he said.

City lost 3-0 to Arsenal in last Sunday’s Community Shield in Cardiff and before Sunday’s visit of Bournemouth for their Premier League opener, Maresca said the critical reaction to the loss had been expected.

“It was good, and normal. It is normal that you are upset straight after the game. We were all upset,” said the manager. “We wanted to win, we didn’t win so it’s a normal reaction but after Tuesday we started to prepare for Bournemouth, you have to switch off one thing and focus on the next one. It was two days where we were not happy and now the focus has to be Bournemouth.”

Maresca has been pleased with how the players are training now he is in charge and not Guardiola. “Since day one the attitude has been very good,” he said. “For them it is not easy. When you work with the same person every day then change, it changes everything.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“I am an actor and I work with the same director, and we make movies for 10 years. Suddenly the director changes, me as the actor I’m still thinking in the same way as I was with the previous director but now the director is new so I need to adapt. It’s complicated, it’s not easy. It’s not an excuse but it requires a little bit of time, but we need to compete as soon as possible.”

Maresca has an ideal size for his squad. “We have three or four academy players that will stay with us because they impressed me in pre-season. Kaden [Braithwaite], [Floyd] Samba and Ryan McAidoo. Then, for me personally we need around 21-22 players. Around 20 players plus these three young players full of energy – we are happy.”

Sports.title: Carrick tells Manchester United to keep calm and carry on after Hull humbling
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick says he will not overreact, but has called for improvement after Manchester United started the season with a 2-0 defeat at Hull. United lost their opening game for the fourth time in the past seven years as Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy took advantage of poor defending from set-pieces.

The United head coach presented a professional exterior despite United’s performance not reaching the desired standard as they were deservedly beaten by Hull, who finished sixth in the Championship last season.

“I’m talking to you quite calmly, but I’m not exactly calm inside and enjoying the day, so there’s a big difference,” he said. “I played [for United] for a long time. You don’t get to play here for a long time without just going day by day, the results, the ups and downs, but you just carry on as normal.

“It’s 100% not that, and trust me, it’s not that. It just doesn’t mean that we all have to shout and scream and come out and create some chaos just because of it. Inside we’re hurting and we need to get better. But the calmness doesn’t mean there’s no emotion in it, for sure.”

He added: “The result’s the result. We got beat, we’re hurt and it’s not a nice feeling. It doesn’t mean it’s going to change the whole direction of how we’re going as a team or as a football club.

“It’s one game and results can happen in football, we all understand that. It’s not nice when they do, but it does happen.”

View image in fullscreen Manchester United’s Bruno Fernandes (left) looks dejected after the match against Hull City Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

United barely threatened throughout the 90 minutes. “Same mistakes as we did last season, every away game,” Bruno Fernandes said. “We gave too much of the ball to them, in the first 20 minutes the goalkeeper had more touches on the ball, too much time. We need to press a little bit more, be more aggressive, and set-plays – we need to work on it, to be more aggressive and try not to concede these types of goals.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Hull’s head coach, Sergej Jakirovic, said he and his backroom staff had spotted a weakness in the way United defended set-pieces, but would not divulge his “secret” that helped to expose it.

Hull are strongly tipped for relegation and their supporters sung “are you watching Joe Cole?” during the match after the pundit mocked their chances of survival. “I don’t have any problems with critics with opinions,” Jakirovic said. “We tried to prove them wrong and today we won the game. Now it’s 37 to go, so we will try to continue like this. I’m very, very happy because of all the people in the club.”

Sports.title: talkSPORT tips – Best football bets and expert advice for Sunday 23 August

Sports.title: Jean-Philippe Mateta takes Crystal Palace dispute to FIFA as Premier League side submit enquiry
Sports.content:
Jean-Philippe Mateta has raised a Crystal Palace contract dispute with FIFA, talkSPORT understands.

The 29-year-old has challenged the remaining ten months of his deal at Palace, which expires in June 2027.



2 Mateta has taken his contract dispute at Palace to FIFA Credit: Getty

The Frenchman first joined the club on an 18-month loan from Mainz in January 2021, with the move made permanent a year later.

This is when he signed a four-and-a-half year contract that included the option of an extra 12 months, which Palace activated in 2024.

However, this additional year is what is being disputed by Mateta.

talkSPORT understands that a Premier League tribunal over the contest was held midway through last season - which didn't go in the player's favour.



He subsequently took his case to the FIFA, but it is understood that Mateta's contract at Selhurst Park remains binding.

Is Mateta subject to any interest from Premier League clubs?

Aston Villa are understood to have enquired about a potential move for Mateta this summer.



Unai Emery's side could lose Ollie Watkins before the window shuts on September 1 amid interest from Al Hilal.

Watkins is open to joining the Saudi Pro League side after spending six seasons at Villa.



However, whilst Mateta is an option for Villa, Nicolas Jackson remains as their priority target.

Chelsea have set an asking price of around £65million for the Senegal international, who spent last season on loan at Bayern Munich.

2 Villa are keen on Mateta, but Jackson is their top target Credit: Getty

A move would see Jackson and Emery reunite after they previously worked together at Villarreal.



Meanwhile, Villa are closing in on the signing of Leon Goretzka.

The midfielder is currently a free agent after leaving Bayern earlier this summer.

Goretzka is set to undergo his medical next week after reaching a verbal agreement with Villa.

Their interest follows the unsuccessful pursuit of Joao Palhinha, who has now joined Benfica.

Villa begin their Premier League campaign away at Brighton on Sunday.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick has been sold short by Manchester United board – but no amount of money can buy passion
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick has been sold short by Manchester United board – but no amount of money can buy passion

So maybe Michael Carrick is not the Messiah after all or maybe he has simply been left short by his paymasters.

Carrick was rightly heralded for leading Manchester United into the Champions League last season, taking more points even than title-winning Mikel Arteta after replacing the hapless Ruben Amorim.



4 United have lose their opening Premier League fixture in successive seasons Credit: AFP

But it took less than 40 minutes of the new season for Carrick’s halo to well and truly slip as United were mauled by a Tigers side written off by many (not me!) as relegation fodder.

Carrick made to rue squad selection?

Carrick’s bold pre-match calls to put his faith in the still raw Ayden Heaven and to leave out Kobbie Mainoo in preference for a central midfield pairing of Andre Santos and Youri Tielemans backfired spectacularly.

Heaven and centre-back partner Harry Maguire were given the runaround by the wily Ollie McBurnie while Santos and Tielemans were frankly useless.



Carrick’s hand was also forced at the top end of the pitch due to an untimely injury to Amad Diallo, meaning Bryan Mbeumo, who has excelled as a striker in pre-season, started out wide with Matheus Cunha as a false number nine.

Cunha took the title literally!

Carrick also left Marcus Rashford on the bench until half-time and Patrick Dorgu was another passenger as the visitors conceded two set piece goals in the space of 21 disastrous minutes.



In contrast to his opposite number, it was a tactical masterclass from Hull gaffer Sergej Jakirovic, who was content to let United dominate the ball, knowing his side could exploit their obvious defensive weaknesses on the counter.

It was the recipe for the Tigers’ unexpected promotion success last season and worked to perfection against a side who has more than 71 per cent possession with next to zero penetration.



Even the half-time addition of Marcus Rashford, who at least looked like he wanted to run at Hull’s defence, could not prevent United slipping to their first ever Premier League defeat in this fixture.

Fellow second half replacement Benjamin Sesko could be playing until the middle of next week and still not look like winning a header against the hosts’ brilliantly-drilled back five.

4 Tielemans and Santos failed to show why they should be United's starting pivot Credit: Getty

4 Mbeumo didn't have his shooting boots on at the MKM Stadium Credit: Getty



United lacked the passion needed to grind out result

What Hull lack in quality, and it is worth pointing out goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis and goal-scoring defender Nobel Mendy both impressed on their Premier League debuts, they more than make up for in heart.

A little over a decade ago Matt Crooks was playing for League Two Accrington Stanley.

The former United trainee and Old Trafford season ticket holder showed a willingness to run and dig in that the £50m Santos simply could not match while the veteran McBurnie’s work ethic left all of United’s supposed ‘superstar’ forwards in the shade.

Hull could have signed £50,000 Regan Slater, whose free-kick set up Mendy’s match-clinching second goal, 1400 times over for the £70million United have just agreed to pay Brighton for Carlos Baleba.



That is why this felt like such a humbling opening day for Carrick and his players, although not all the blame should be laid at the manager’s door.

Director of football Jason Wilcox looked pretty pleased with himself standing outside the boardroom pre-match, presumably having clinched the signature of long-term target Baleba for a reduced fee.

4 United are looking to return to winning ways next weekend against newly-promoted Ipswich at Old Trafford Credit: Getty

Wilcox’s post-match expression told a different story and Baleba’s arrival cannot solve all of United’s problems when it comes to keeping clean sheets.



Luke Shaw and Maguire both started the Red Devils’ chastening 4-0 defeat at Brentford in Erik ten Hag’s second game in charge some four years ago.

What positions do United need to strengthen in?

United need an upgrade on Shaw at left-back and for his qualities and character, there is a strong argument to be made that if Maguire has not provided the solution to leaking goals during his seven years at the club, then he is part of the issue.

The club have high hopes for Leny Yoro, but he is still to prove himself at this level while both Lisandro Martinez and, even more so, Matthijs de Ligt have been held back by injury.

Wilcox and co have a little over a week of the transfer window left to provide Carrick the tools he needs to make sure this opening day horror show does not become the norm in his first full season in charge.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi declares he is not angry with squad despite ‘worst Tottenham performance’
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi declares he is not angry with squad despite ‘worst Tottenham performance’

Roberto De Zerbi has insisted that he is neither angry nor frustrated with his Tottenham side despite their humiliating defeat to Brentford.

Spurs suffered a shock 3-0 loss in their Premier League opener that has sent them to the bottom of the table.

3 Spurs marked the start of their season with a poor performance at Brentford Credit: Getty

Keane Lewis-Potter, Vitaly Janelt and Michael Kayode all scored as the Bees beat their opponents at home for the first time since 1948.

De Zerbi, who has begun his first full season in charge of Spurs, cast a dejected figure on the bench throughout the 90 minutes.

What has De Zerbi said about Tottenham's defeat?

However, when speaking to talkSPORT after full-time, the Italian was not one to express any irritation with the result.

When asked by Ian Abrahams if he felt angry or frustrated with his team, he simply said: "No, nothing.

"Not frustrated or angry, I'm thinking a lot, what I can do to quickly improve the team.

"In that way, I have my focus."

De Zerbi then added: "To become a team, maybe we need more time, to fight stronger, to be stronger in the duels."

What has been said about Spurs' performance?

Given it's the opening weekend of the season and there is another 37 fixtures for Spurs to play, De Zerbi's calmness may be unsurprising.

However, talkSPORT host Rory Jennings was left stunned with Spurs and their display in west London.

They had just four shots on target from a possible nine and only 18 touches inside the Brentford box.

3 De Zerbi remained calm when reflecting on his side's display Credit: Getty

Jennings explained: "I'm not even talking in hyperbole here, when I think about Tottenham over the last 18 months.

"The performance that we have just watched at Brentford is possibly the worst, or on par, with some of the dreadful performances I have seen from Tottenham under previous managers. What is going on?"

Jennings continued: "De Zerbi had the back end of last season, he's had a summer where I felt like Tottenham really got it right in the transfer market.

"Look, I have no love for Tottenham whatsoever, but I was also conceding that I thought that (they) had a really good window.

"I thought the signing of (Sandro) Tonali was a statement, I thought (Mateus) Fernandes under the nose of Manchester United was exactly what was needed.

"Bringing in (Jan Paul) Van Hecke, elevating that backline, getting rid of (Cristian) Romero felt like a win,

3 Brentford were levels above Spurs and deserved winners Credit: Getty

(Marcos) Senesi was intelligent, (Andy) Robertson was going to set the standards, but I just can't believe it."

Jennings then stated: "This is as bad as a performance I can remember from Tottenham in recent memory, I think it genuinely is."

Four of Spurs' six summer signings started in the defeat to Brentford, and more arrivals could be on their way.

talkSPORT understands they are close to agreeing an £85million deal for Manchester City winger Savinho.

Spurs are also in talks with City for Omar Marmoush as they look set to surpass the £350m mark this summer.

They will be looking to return to winning ways against Charlton in the Carabao Cup second round on Wednesday night, before facing Newcastle next weekend.

Sports.title: Tottenham told to immediately sell player as Spurs go bottom after unwanted 78-year first
Sports.content:
Tottenham told to immediately sell player as Spurs go bottom after unwanted 78-year first

Tottenham Hotspur sit bottom of the table after suffering a 3-0 defeat away at Brentford in their Premier League opener.

Goals from Keane Lewis-Potter and Vitaly Janelt had the Bees two goals up with a little over half an hour played on Saturday evening.



5 Brentford battered Spurs in their Premier League opener on Saturday Credit: AFP

5 De Zerbi watched on in horror as his Spurs side were well beaten Credit: Getty

Brentford then added their third via Michael Kayode in the opening stages of the second half to effectively win the three points.

It could have got even worse for Spurs as they conceded a penalty moments later, but Igor Thiago hit the post.



Defeat for the north Londoners is their joint-worst in an opening match of a Premier League season.

It has come 15 years after they lost 3-0 away to Manchester United.

Spurs have also lost away to Brentford for the first time since 1948 when they were beaten 3-1 at Griffin Park.



And after finishing 17th in back-to-back seasons, Tottenham have once again been battered - despite spending over £230million this window.

What has been said about Spurs' defeat to Brentfod?

talkSPORT's resident Spurs fan Jamie O'Hara was live on the GameDay Phone-In during the match and was, unsurprisingly, fuming.



He took issue with Richarlison, who didn't manage a single shot and committed two fouls during the match.

"You cannot start a Premier League season like that, and I know there's injuries, but that is absolutely disgraceful," ex-Spurs midfielder O'Hara insisted during his half-time analysis.

"With Richarlison, I don't know why this guy is still at our football club, he ain't good enough.

5 Richarlison failed to make an impact at the Gtech Community Stadium Credit: Shutterstock Editorial



5 O'Hara coculdn't believe what he was watching as Spurs were bullied in west London Credit: talkSPORT

"You've got (Dominic) Solanke… I'd rather play James Maddison up front. Like, genuinely, Maddison, I'll play him as a false nine.

"Seriously, Richarlison cannot play for Tottenham anymore, he's nowhere near good enough, get him off the pitch."

O'Hara added: "(Lucas) Bergvall and Richarlison are the reason why we finished 17th for the last two seasons."



Speaking following the full-time whistle, O'Hara then declared that it could be another season of battling relegation if his beloved side don't improve - and fast.

He remarked: "If we play like that we will go down, because you cannot turn up to a football match and play like that, they should be ashamed of themselves.

"That is a disgrace, an absolute disgrace, and we have been scammed once again by Richarlison.

5 Could Spurs be set for another challenging campaign?



"It's so bad, I'm ashamed to be a Spurs fan - one game in.

"How can you give us that on the first day? Absolute guff."

Spurs, who failed to get a shot on target in the first half of a Premier League match for the tenth time since the beginning of last season, arrived at Brentford after a £230m summer spending spree.

And that figure is set to rise to over £300m with Savinho closing in on a move from Manchester City.

Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Andy Robertson and Sandro Tonali were all of the summer arrivals who started.

Mateus Fernandes came off the bench at the start of the second half, but none of Roberto De Zerbi's signings impressed.



Up next for Spurs is a home tie against Newcastle next weekend, while table-toppers Brentford travel to Leeds.

Sports.title: EFL star forced to come off after channelling inner Emmanuel Adebayor against former club
Sports.content:
EFL star forced to come off after channelling inner Emmanuel Adebayor against former club

Bobby Kamwa ran the length of the pitch when celebrating against Newport County - only to be substituted immediately after.

The winger scored his side's fourth goal in their 5-3 victory on Saturday, which claimed their first points of the League Two season.



3 Kamwa opened his account for Bristol Rovers in exquisite fashion against old club Newport Credit: Sky Sports

3 The winger was subject to verbal abuse from the travelling supporters throughout the game Credit: Sky Sports

Kamwa ran onto the end of a fantastic pass from goalkeeper Brad Young, cut onto his right foot and fired into the top right corner.

Starting inside the area, he then sprinted towards the Newport fans, who were positioned at the other end of the Memorial Stadium pitch.



He passionately celebrated in front of his former club's supporters in what appeared to be a recreation of a famous celebration.

Emmanuel Adebayor memorably ran from one end of the pitch at the Etihad Stadium to the other in 2009 when at Manchester City.



He scored in a 4-2 Premier League win over Arsenal, who he had left only weeks beforehand, and enraged their fans with his antics.

Kamwa did the same as objects appeared to be thrown his way as he revelled in his goal, although boss Steve Evans defended the celebration.



What did Evans say about Kamwa?

Speaking to the media afterwards, he hinted that the 26-year-old received some unsavoury remarks during the match.

"Bobby's is a fantastic goal, but some of the comments aimed at Bobby on my left-hand side today have got no place in football. That's just where it is.

"And I have a lot of time for the ownership model at Newport County, and the fans have always been fair with me and give me a bit of banter, etc.

"But some of them, it'll be individuals, possibly, that overstepped the line.



3 Adebayor's famous celebration now has its own League Two version Credit: Getty

"So when Bobby sticks a goal at that end, Bobby's a little Yorkshire boy who's got character and a bit of fight, a bit of spirit.

"I read his words in the Bristol press earlier this week when he said, if they give me some proper stick, I'll celebrate.

"If they behave themselves, I wouldn't, you know, if they're not giving Bobby some outrageous chants, then I don't think Bobby would have been running 100 yards."



Evans then revealed that Kamwa's celebration took a lot out of him, so much so that he was brought off for the final 11 minutes.

"He had to come off afterwards," he explained. "He was very tired."

Bristol Rovers, who lost 3-2 to York City on the opening weekend, are tenth in League Two thanks to the win over Newport.

They are playing in their second consecutive season in the fourth-tier following League One relegation in the 2024/25 campaign.

Sports.title: ‘Absolutely pathetic’ – EFL club told to have emergency board meeting and sack manager
Sports.content:
Adrian Durham has urged Norwich to sack manager Philippe Clement after his 'pathetic' rant about VAR before his side's defeat to Millwall.

The Belgian's nightmare start to the season continued on Saturday, as the Canaries fell to a demoralising 3-0 loss at the Den.

3 Philippe Clement's Norwich have no points on the board after their first two Championship games Credit: Getty

A Tairyk Arconte double before Luke Cundle's late goal made it two defeats from two for Norwich this campaign, who were reduced to ten men after Jose Cordoba was dismissed in the second half.

This leaves Clement's side 23rd in the Championship already, with only Southampton below them thanks to their four-point deduction.

Norwich's drubbing at the hands of Millwall came just a week after their opening-day defeat to Blackburn was marred by controversy.

The Baggies ran out 2-1 winners at Carrow Road, but were handed a slice of good fortune when Aune Heggebo's opener came via him diverting the ball into the net with his hand.

Despite the appeals of the Norwich players, the goal was allowed to stand by referee Tim Robinson.

The goal quickly went viral on social media, leading to calls for VAR to be introduced, while Heggebo was later handed a two-game ban by the EFL for ‘successful deception of a match official’.

What did Clement say about VAR?

A day before Norwich's clash with Millwall, Clement delivered a passionate rant calling for VAR to be introduced to the Championship, naming all 71 countries that use the technology.

In a seven-minute long monologue, the ex-Rangers boss said: “I think the league creates its own problems by not having VAR.

“I didn’t want to go into that after the game because you want to focus on the team and the things we could do better, and clearly there are things the referees could have done better.

“But I know it’s real time it goes fast, and there are errors made by human beings.

3 Tairyk Arconte's double saw Millwall put Norwich to the sword on Saturday Credit: Getty

“That’s why there’s VAR. So the next morning, you’re still gutted about things, and then I asked my analyst to look up, in which leagues around the world, there is VAR.

"So that’s why I have this list.”

Clement then stopped the press conference to read out all 71 countries that use VAR, even taking time to specify which nations have it across more than one division – unlike England.

He added: “So all these leagues have VAR. There are countries that never played in a World Cup here.

“It’s madness for me that there’s no VAR in the Championship.”

What has Adrian Durham said about Clement?

Less than 24 hours on from Clement's VAR plea, his rant backfired as Norwich were well beaten at the Den, and talkSPORT's Durham was less than impressed with their manager's behaviour.

3 Norwich have now shipped in five goals from their opening two Championship games Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Reacting to the result on air, Durham said: "Millwall 3-0 Norwich City was the full-time score.

“Millwall looked really good when I was watching them last week at Bristol City and they backed it up with a big home win against Norwich who had Jose Cordoba sent off at.

Delivering a scathing verdict on Clement, Durham then fumed: “Any wonder Norwich were battered at Millwall.

“Philippe Clement the manager told his analysts to find out all the countries that have VAR instead of using his analysts to find out about his opponents Millwall.

“Absolutely pathetic rant about VAR - should have led to an emergency board meeting at Norwich and he should no longer be the manager, but that's just my opinion.“

Clement took over at Norwich in November 2025, nine months on from his sacking by Rangers, and guided his side to a ninth-place finish last term.

And while the Canaries were tipped for a play-off push before the season began, their manager's main focus now will be getting some points on the board as they look to get out of the Championship relegation zone.

Sports.title: Hull fans send clear message to Joe Cole during upset win over Man United as manager hits back
Sports.content:
Hull fans send clear message to Joe Cole during upset win over Man United as manager hits back

Hull City fans have had the first laugh and are hoping they have the last one too.

The Tigers announced their return to the Premier League with a superb 2-0 win over Manchester United in the lunchtime kick off.

4 Nobel Mendy's header fired Hull into a deserved 2-0 lead shortly before half time Credit: Getty

4 Hull fans were delirious after their side's perfect start to the season Credit: AFP

First-half goals from Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy were enough to see off Michael Carrick’s men at the MKM Stadium and claim three valuable points in the club’s quest for survival.

And there was a little bit of history made as Sergej Jakirovic became the first Hull manager to beat Manchester United in the Premier League.

But attention from the stands quickly turned to TNT Sports pundit Joe Cole after comments he made about the club’s chances of survival earlier this week alongside our very own Carlton Cole, who refused to apologise on last night's Sports Bar Weekender.

Former Chelsea and West Ham midfielder Joe Cole revealed that he intentionally ignored a request from TNT Sports to cover Hull’s Premier League opener.

Speaking on the 'Dressing Room' podcast alongside Carlton Cole, he also predicted that the club are certain to be relegated at the end of the season.

And it’s fair to say that his comments did not go down well with the Premier League new boys.

That led to Hull owner Acun Ilicali publicly slamming Cole’s comments live on talkSPORT on Friday.

And that was backed up by a packed out MKM Stadium on Saturday who called out the pundit during the match.

Fans were heard chanting: “Are you watching Joe Cole?"

The chants took place as Hull fans revelled in their side’s brilliant performance to sweep aside Carrick’s expensively-assembled side.

4 TNT Sports pundit Joe Cole came under fire this week for his comments on Hull Credit: Getty

Hull will use their detractors as a source of motivation

After the match, Jakirovic also had his say on Cole’s comments and his side’s objectives for the season.

“It’s a big motivation for us because somebody underestimated you, especially from an ex-player,” Jakirovic told talkSPORT.

“Because you were a professional and know how difficult it is to get promotion from the Championship to the Premier League. It’s not easy.

“This is a big motivation for us and we will try to prove all these people wrong. This is our main goal this season.”

Cole did receive support over his comments from namesake and former teammate Carlton Cole.

The ex-Premier League striker took to Instagram urging fans not to take Cole's comments too seriously and passed it off as 'banter'.

4 Sergej Jakirovic says he will use Cole's comments to rally his troops this season Credit: Getty

"We've come under a bit of fire at the Dressing Room. The Hull City fans are not happy with us,"

"Listen, a bit of back and forth, a bit of banter, it's alright. It's not the end of the world. One man's opinion doesn't make it right, doesn't make it real.

"You might be disappointed with that opinion, but it's alright. That's the whole point of football. Yes, I did belly laugh when he said that you snuck in at the back door. I did. Come on, it's funny. I'm laughing at my mate's joke. I can do that.

"Joe thinks that you won't stay up and it's alright if you don't stay up. It's okay. You've done well to get to this point.

"I love Hull City," he continued. "I've got admiration for Hull City. My son was there. He's now at Middlesbrough, but when I look back, the fans were amazing.

He added: "So what I want from you is to suggest a forfeit. If you do stay up, or anybody that thinks Hull's going to stay up, send your suggestions in for a forfeit for Joe Cole."

With three points on the board, Hull quickly turn their attention to the Carabao Cup and a midweek trip to Championship side Stoke City.

Then it is back to Premier League duty with a trip to fellow promoted club Coventry before clashes against Aston Villa, Chelsea and Newcastle.

Sports.title: Alan Shearer hits out at 'dreadful' Man United and claims Michael Carrick's side are 'not fit' after dismal opening day defeat by Hull City - as legend pinpoints the area stars 'offered nothing'
Sports.content:
Alan Shearer hits out at 'dreadful' Man United and claims Michael Carrick's side are 'not fit' after dismal opening day defeat by Hull City - as legend pinpoints the area stars 'offered nothing'

Alan Shearer has taken aim at Manchester United following their 'dreadful' performance at Hull City, with the Match of the Day pundit accusing Michael Carrick's side of lacking fitness.

The Red Devils wilted at newly-promoted Hull on Saturday, with goals from Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy handing the newcomers a 2-0 victory.

The manner of United's defeat has caused alarm among supporters and pundits, with Shearer offering a withering verdict on the BBC's flagship football show on Saturday night.

'Man United were dreadful in all positions I thought, particularly upfront, they offered nothing,' he said. 'At times I struggled to work out what they were trying to do.

'[There is] so much to work on, so much to improve, I know it was the first game of the season but there was without a doubt a lack of energy, they just didn't look fit, Manchester United.

'There was only one team who were going to win that today from the very first minute, you saw the energy, you saw the intensity.

Alan Shearer has torn into Man United's opening day performance against Hull City

Man United put in a woeful display at Hull City to lose their opening game of the season

'That would be the worrying thing - you know that as a team going away from home to a newly promoted team, you know what you're going to get and you have to match them as a minimum and Man Utd didn't today. They couldn't live with them.'

The defeat at Hull was Carrick's first match in charge since being given the first-team head coach role on a permanent basis - having impressed during his interim tenure following the sacking of Ruben Amorim.

Carrick has refused to hit the panic button following Saturday's result.

'We haven't lost many games in six, seven months,' the United boss said.

'So again, I get it, we've lost today and I understand there's questions to be asked, but it doesn't mean everything's wrong because we've lost a game.

'We've done a lot of good things and we did some good things today, but it gets lost, and I understand it'll get lost, but it doesn't get lost from our point of view.

'There's definitely issues playing against different systems, so we have got to find the answers for that. But just because we lose one game it doesn't mean that everything needs to be dissected and it's wrong from our point of view.'

Carrick is rarely ruffled win, lose, or draw, but behind his calm demeanour here was a coach hurting at seeing his side totally outplayed.

Shearer claims United do not look fit as he sounded the alarm on Match of the Day

'I'm talking to you quite calm, but I'm not exactly calm inside and enjoying the day, you know?

'So there's a big difference. I played here for a long time. You don't get to play here for a long time without just going day by day, the results, the ups and downs, but you just carry on as normal. It's 100% not that; trust me, it's not that.

'It just doesn't mean that we all have to shout and scream and come out and create some chaos just because of it.

'Inside we're hurting. The boys know we need to get better, but the calmness doesn't mean that there's no emotion in it, for sure.'

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso backs 'world class' Cole Palmer to return to form this season and refuses to confirm if Robert Sanchez will be his starting keeper
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso is determined to unlock the 'world class' side of Cole Palmer after Chelsea's playmaker suffered his first injury-plagued season to the detriment of his club.

The 2025-26 campaign saw Palmer struggle with a groin problem in particular but he also had other issues, including fracturing his little toe after stubbing it on a door at home. His limited influence contributed to Chelsea finishing 10th in the Premier League.

Before opening their campaign away at Fulham, Alonso spoke of how Palmer is pushing to avoid a recurrence of his previous injuries. 'Cole is determined to enjoy his football,' Chelsea's manager said. 'He wants to be fit. He wants to feel healthy.

'He wants to have a good connection with the players around him. We have this goal. If we are able to reach him and he feels that flow in the game and connects well with the players, I'm sure his level is top class, world class, and that he will have a great season.

Xabi Alonso is desperate to get the best out of Chelsea playmaker Cole Palmer this season

'Sometimes you need to go through a moment with an injury or whatever to learn from that.

'Cole has gone through a difficult period with an injury and now he's working really hard to have the prevention to not feel those symptoms back. Since the first day, he's been working really hard to avoid that.'

Chelsea's trip to Fulham last season saw Marc Cucurella dismissed after 22 minutes as the 10-man visitors lost 2-1. The Blues received eight red cards in 2025-26 – the most of any club in the Premier League as their campaign was plagued by poor discipline.

Alonso has fined players before at previous clubs and said when asked how he will respond to reds at Chelsea: 'It depends on the context. You can have a red card. It's football. It can happen. There is always a context for everything but I don't have written rules for this kind of thing.

'We need to assess the particular cases. But for sure, having emotional control gives you the game control that we want to avoid these kinds of situations.'

Robert Sanchez is expected to start in goal versus Fulham over Mike Penders, though Xabi Alonso refused to confirm that. 'We want healthy competition in all the positions,' Alonso said. 'We will see. The pitch is the boss of everything. I don't decide. The players need to show me.'

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca admits Manchester City urgently need to find a 'new Rodri' this summer - as race to complete deals before Deadline Day heats up
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca believes Manchester City can find ‘the new Rodri’ this month as they move on without their linchpin.

The Spain captain left for Barcelona last week, with City expected to wrap up a deal for Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi during the transfer window.

With Elliot Anderson already signed, Maresca is confident that the new recruits can fill the void left by Rodri.

And Maresca pointed to the fact that the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner had never lifted major silverware before joining City in 2019 – underlining that they can mould signings into becoming the best in class.

‘Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri,’ Maresca said. ‘How do we solve the problem? Try to find the new Rodri.

‘Before he arrived, he didn't win the Ballon d'Or, he didn't win the Champions League, he didn't win the Club World Cup. He joined the club then he achieved many important things.’

Enzo Maresca believes Man City can find their successor to Rodri by the end of this month

The Man City boss believes new recruits can fill the void left by the Spanish star

Rodri had made it clear that he wanted to leave the Etihad Stadium and Maresca has been unequivocal that any player eying a move away can depart, mirroring the principles of predecessor Pep Guardiola.

And the Italian claimed that life will move on, reeling off how City replaced previous big-name stars.

‘When Sergio [Aguero] was here, everyone was worried and Erling [Haaland] arrived,’ he added. ‘Fernandinho? Rodri arrived. It is just about this.

‘When they leave, you need to be good in recruiting the next one. They are all similar, David [Silva], Kevin [De Bruyne], Fernandinho, Rodri, Erling. It is normal, it is change, it is not a problem, go again and try to do the right things.’

Meanwhile, Maresca confirmed that he is looking for a squad of around 20 outfield players. City currently have 19 senior players, excluding summer signing Jeremy Monga, but the number includes the likes of Tottenham target Omar Marmoush, Newcastle target Nico Gonzalez and Jack Grealish.

‘It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, that is for sure,’ Maresca added. ‘But we need to adapt. There are 10 days to go, hopefully we can do the things that we need to do.

‘The normal thing in the transfer window is that you have to wait until the last week, because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money. At the end, we’ll have all the squad here for sure it will be different.’

Sports.title: Carlos Baleba to undergo Man United medical TODAY as Crystal Palace slap down Jean-Philippe Mateta enquiry and Aston Villa agree terms with free agent Leon Goretzka: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Carlos Baleba to undergo Man United medical TODAY as Crystal Palace slap down Jean-Philippe Mateta enquiry and Aston Villa agree terms with free agent Leon Goretzka: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Villa agree terms for Goretzka

Aston Villa have agreed terms with former Bayern Munich midfielder Leon Goretzka on a free transfer.

Pending a medical, the 31-year-old is expected to sign a three-year deal this week.

Taylor Harwood-Bellis was left out of Southampton's squad to face Stoke City amid Villa's interest in the defender.

Aston Villa have agreed terms with former Bayern Munich midfielder Leon Goretzka on a free transfer

Villa have had an enquiry for Jean-Philippe Mateta knocked back by Crystal Palace.

Unai Emery's team are hunting a centre-forward with Al-Hilal pushing hard to sign Ollie Watkins.

Villa are also ready to bid for Nicolas Jackson from Chelsea. Watkins has also been offered a new deal at Villa.

Napoli sign Chelsea star on loan

Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile has joined Napoli on a loan deal, with an option to buy.

The loan fee is worth £2.5million and could rise to £3.4m with add-ons. The option price is around £23m.

Chelsea could receive more than £26m from the deal if Badiashile moves permanently. They valued him at £30m in this window.

Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile has joined Napoli on a loan deal, with an option to buy

Napoli are also one of the clubs keen on Chelsea's Marc Guiu. He is weighing up options from Spain and Germany too.

Hull City are exploring a loan for Chelsea midfielder Dario Essugo who is also wanted at Strasbourg.

Wrexham eye up move for Millwall's Azeez

Wrexham are exploring a move for Millwall forward Femi Azeez.

The exciting 25-year-old also has interest from Brighton and Hull City.

The Robins are hoping the Nigeria international will be attracted by their ambitious project despite Millwall being rival promotion contenders.

Wrexham are also looking at Ipswich Town attacking midfielder Anis Mehmeti.

The 25-year-old Albania international only joined in January from Bristol City for £3.5m and scored his first goal for the club against Wrexham.

The move would mean him giving up the opportunity of Premier League football now though Wrexham hope to be there in a year's time.

Meanwhile, Wrexham's move for free agent defender Axel Tuanzebe looks to be off.

The exciting 25-year-old also has interest from Brighton and Hull City

Brighton enquire about Hull target Hernandez

Brighton have asked about Deportivo La Coruna winger Yeremay Hernandez.

The 23-year-old has been in the UK to talk to Hull City who have been trying to sign him but Brighton are exploring a move also.

Hull owner Acun Ilicali said: 'We have to get the club side done and Yeremay also wants to come but it is a very vital, critical decision for himself.

'This deal is a very hard deal but we are somewhere where it looks positive. He is young boy and it would change his life completely so he wanted to see where he would come. We will see in three, four days if this deal will be done or not. If it happens it will be a record for sure.'

Brighton remain in talks with Liverpool over the sale of winger Yankuba Minteh.

Though the 22-year-old wants the move, the clubs are some distance apart on valuation with Brighton wanting over £70m to reflect market prices.

The 23-year-old has been in the UK to talk to Hull City who have been trying to sign him but Brighton are exploring a move also

Blues keep tabs on Conceicao amid interest in Neto

Juventus winger Francisco Conceicao is back on Chelsesa's radar in case they sell Pedro Neto.

Conceicao was bought from Porto for £36million and Juventus would want some profit on their outlay for the 23-year-old Portugal international.

Neto has interest from Al Hilal, Tottenham and Manchester City but Chelsea are asking £100m.

They also have an offer from Roma for Jamie Gittens but so far that's too low, as a loan with option.

Conceicao is quick, technically good and robust for his diminutive stature.

Juventus would look to utilise any money from Conceicao for targets such as Manchester United's Joshua Zirkzee.

Juventus winger Conceicao is back on Chelsesa's radar in case they sell Pedro Neto, with Al Hilal, Tottenham and Manchester City all interested in Neto

Magpies reignite interest in Spurs' Gray

Newcastle United have rekindled interest in Tottenham's versatile midfielder Archie Gray.

The 20-year-old is still very much part of coach Roberto de Zerbi's plans as he can cover various positions though midfield is his preference. He has also captained the team during pre-season.

Newcastle are speaking to Manchester City about Nico Gonzalez but Gray is also someone they admire.

After losing so much quality they are exploring a number of options to strengthen their squad and add Premier League experience.

Since joining Spurs from Leeds for £40million, Gray has made 81 appearances, often filling in at centre-back and right-back as well as midfield.

Tottenham will need to consider sales to offset their substantial summer spending, though they would prefer to sell others. Gray is valued over £60m.

Since joining Spurs from Leeds for £40million, Gray has made 81 appearances, often filling in at centre-back and right-back as well as midfield and has captained the side during pre-season

Joao Pedro signs eight-year Blues contract

Joao Pedro has signed his new Chelsea contract until 2034.

Chelsea have been determined to keep the Brazil international after he emerged as a target for Barcelona early in the summer.

The Brazil international joined the Blues from Brighton in July 2025 and made an immediate impact, scoring in the Club World Cup semi-final and final as Chelsea were crowned world champions.

His form continued into his first full season at Stamford Bridge, with the forward scoring 20 goals in all competitions.

While the club are willing to listen to offers for Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson, the 24-year-old was named Chelsea's new No 9 last week.

Joao Pedro said: 'I am very happy to sign a new contract with Chelsea. I always dreamed of playing for a big club, and it means a lot to me to give my long-term commitment to this club.

'Everyone is very excited for this season. We know we can achieve a lot of things. We have a great team, we have a coach who wants to win and has won already.'

Joao Pedro, who has signed a fresh eight-year deal at Chelsea, said: 'I always dreamed of playing for a big club, it means a lot to me to give my long-term commitment to this club'

Baleba prepares for Man United medical

Carlos Baleba is due to undergo his medical today ahead of completing his £70million move from Brighton to Manchester United.

The 22-year-old is recovering from an ankle ligament injury but is expected to be fit towards the end of next month.

The deal was agreed early on Friday evening at £65m plus add-ons and a sell-on clause.

Newcastle target given the green light for move

Newcastle target Nico Gonzalez has been told by Enzo Maresca and Hugo Viana that he can leave Manchester City.

Gonzalez was ready to fight for his place but with City looking to sign two more midfielders they are realistic about his prospects of playing regularly.

Newcastle believe he is open to the move and is emerging as their priority on a shortlist of three targets.

Nico Gonzalez has been told that he can move from Man City amid interest from Newcastle

Newcastle have also registered interest in Christopher Nkunku of AC Milan, though RB Leipzig are more active on the situation as it stands.

Man City's talks for Ayyoub Bouaddi are continuing, though Lille have been pushing for optimum price on the 18-year-old.

Man City forward Omar Marmoush is still expected to complete his move to Tottenham.

Liverpool fledgling books Levente loan deal

Liverpool defensive prospect Ifeanyi Ndukwe is joining Levante on loan.

The 18-year-old does not qualify for a work permit in England as yet, so is having to be loaned out to play competitive football.

The Austrian youth international has excelled during Liverpool's pre-season and the club have high hopes for his future.

First team football in a top league such as LaLiga is viewed as an integral next step.

He has travelled to Valencia to complete terms. Ndukwe also had interest from clubs in Portugal, France and Germany.

City defender to join Coventry

Manchester City defender Stephen Mfuni is in talks to join Coventry City on loan.

The 18-year-old, who can play left back and centre back, was a target for Watford who had him on loan last season.
