Sports.title: Norris beats Mercedes pair to Dutch Grand Prix pole position | 2026 Dutch Grand Prix qualifying report
Sports.content:
Lando Norris claimed pole position for the second grand prix in a row, denying the Mercedes drivers in a closely-fought session.

The front-running drivers hurried to complete their final runs as rain threatened to fall during the deciding moments of Q3. Norris, who held provisional pole position ahead of George Russell following the first runs, raced to keep his rival behind him after they joined the track for their final runs.

Both followed Andrea Kimi Antonelli in the other Mercedes who went fastest with his final run. Norris beat his time by more than a tenth of a second, however, then Russell split the pair of them. Oscar Piastri ensured Mercedes-powered cars filled the top four places.

The Ferrari drivers gambled with the weather and completed their final runs after their rivals. Lewis Hamilton beat his team mate’s time and the pair will share the third row of the grid. The Red Bull duo claimed the fourth row, Liam Lawson impressively lapping just a tenth of a second slower than Max Verstappen on his return to the team.

Yuki Tsunoda could not join his team mate Arvid Lindblad in Q3 on his return to Formula 1. Lindblad took 10th on the grid behind Gabriel Bortoleto, who scraped through the first round after a slow first run and a significant snap of oversteer at the exit of Tarzan.

Neither Alpine driver made the cut for Q3, including Pierre Gasly who had the benefit of the team’s upgrade. He fell short by a tenth of a second. Nico Hulkenberg also dropped out in Q2.

Alexander Albon was the only Williams driver to reach Q2, beating team mate Carlos Sainz Jnr by a few hundredths of a second. Both of the upgraded Aston Martins went out in the first round, ahead of Oliver Bearman and the two Cadillacs.

Sports.title: McLaren’s car is “terrible” in low-speed corners – Norris | Formula 1
Sports.content:
McLaren’s performance in Zandvoort highlights their car’s weakness in slow corners, says Lando Norris.

The reigning world champion won the previous round at the Hungaroring, a circuit which has several low-to-medium-speed corners, but he believes the slower mix of corners at Zandvoort is a problem for the MCL40.

“We knew in Budapest we’re very good in high-speed corners and we’re pretty terrible in slow speed, but we still managed to win,” he said. “Here there’s a lot more of the very, very slow speed and more of our problems show. So [it’s] not a surprise at all. It’s exactly what we expected.”

McLaren have brought further upgrades for their car in Zandvoort. Norris said these have performed as expected but the team still has a significant deficit to its rivals at some circuits.

“They’ve done exactly as they should, so I’m very happy,” he said. “We still managed to progress.

“It’s just [in] certain areas we’re just nowhere near quick enough. The slow speed, we’ve just struggled the whole weekend and seems clearly the weakness we have in the car at the minute. I feel if we still went back to Monaco now, we’re going to be shocking, as we were.

“So I think we’ve clearly progressed a lot, and especially in medium and high-speed, which is why we’re quick here, why we were so quick in Budapest. It wasn’t like we were quick everywhere in Budapest, and that’s why we won. The slow speed, we were still slower than Ferrari and matching Mercedes just about.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“So we still have weaknesses, even though we managed to win one race. It’s just the strengths really shone there, and here it’s just the deficit is too big in the slow speed.”

Norris qualified second on the grid for today’s sprint race alongside George Russell but fell to third behind Charles Leclerc. He doubts McLaren can make any significant changes to the car’s poor performance in low-speed corners for the time being.

“There’s just nothing we can do about it now. It’s just how the car is for the time being.

“That’s where we still have to focus as a team. We’ll try and get everything out of it. I feel like I still did a good job today, even with the P3.

“It’s just [that] I want to be fighting for top spot and be fighting and going forward and catching George and putting him under pressure rather than trying to survive in every slow-speed corner and fighting for my life.

“So I’m very happy with the team and the progress we made, and the upgrades have all worked, and they’ve allowed me to be P3 today. But we just need more if we want to fight for a championship.”

YUKI KEY MESSAGING Happy to be back racing on track

I’m here to support both teams when…

As always, I’ll do my best to secure… POTENTIAL QUESTIONS How did you find out you were going… Laurent called me (TBC based on…) What was your first reaction when you… Obviously excited to be back on… mend, but feel prepared to… Did you expect to get another F1 race… Anything can happen in F1. Sports.title: Lopez Wants Three Unifications Without Facing One Mandatory
Sports.content:
During his post-fight press conference, Lopez said:

“I got three fights with DAZN, and all of them are the road to undisputed. We’re going right to every world title. We’re not taking no title defense, no nothing. Whoever’s next, we’re going for him.”

A unification technically includes a defense of the belts involved, but Lopez’s meaning was clear. He does not plan to face an ordinary mandatory or ranked challenger between attempts to collect the other titles. If that plan proceeds, it will consume well over a year. Each fight requires negotiations between promoters, networks and boxing organizations before the participants complete training camps and recover afterward. Lopez also left the Romero fight with a cut over his right eyebrow that may delay his return.

The first unification depends on another event. Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn are scheduled to fight on September 12, after which the winner will need time to recover and negotiate with Lopez. The next stage against Liam Paro or Devin Haney requires another lengthy round of discussions.

Completing all three fights may leave contenders in several organizations waiting 12 to 18 months. Some will be forced into additional bouts to protect their rankings while the champion moves from one financially attractive unification to another.

Unifications often receive priority because reducing the number of champions is supposed to benefit boxing. That principle becomes difficult to defend when it is used repeatedly to prevent every other challenger from receiving an opportunity.

Granting one exception for a major fight is understandable. Three consecutive exceptions create a separate set of rules for the boxer who generates the most money. Ranked contenders must keep winning while Teofimo remains protected from facing any of them.

The strategy also depends on Lopez winning every fight. A loss transfers the collected titles to another champion, who may then request additional exceptions for more lucrative bouts. The waiting challengers must begin the same process again with someone new.

The schedule Teofimo described requires approval from more than DAZN. The WBA and the other organizations must authorize each step. If they permit three straight unifications without requiring a mandatory defense, the “road to undisputed” will become another example of boxing’s business interests overriding its competitive structure.

Sports.title: Catterall Threatens Teofimo Lopez’s Big-Money Welterweight Plans
Sports.content:
A majority decision over Rolando Romero at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas gave Lopez the belt. His steady pressure, jab and body work earned scores of 116-112 and 115-113, while the third judge returned a 114-114 card.

Watching from outside the ring, Catterall made his opinion clear on social media.

“I beat either of these pair no doubt in my mind,” said Catterall on X about Teofimo and Rolly.

That confidence is not difficult to understand after Lopez’s welterweight debut. Romero spent long stretches moving backward and waiting for one power counter. His low output allowed Lopez to win rounds through activity without producing a dominant offensive performance.

When Romero finally attacked in the fifth, he hurt Teofimo with a left hand and opened a cut over his right eyebrow. Lopez recovered and regained control, but he never seriously hurt Romero despite landing the cleaner punches for much of the fight.

A more difficult test comes from Catterall. The British southpaw will not concede as many quiet rounds. His timing, counters and disciplined defense can disrupt Teofimo’s lead hand and force him to reset before attacking. He also has the patience to punish the wide punches Teofimo throws when he becomes frustrated.

The WBA ordered its Super champion to face the winner of Jack Catterall vs. Shakhram Giyasov within 180 days of their May 23 bout. Catterall won that fight and holds the secondary WBA welterweight title, placing him next in line for a consolidation bout. The period ends on November 19, although the WBA has not issued a new public order naming Lopez since he defeated Romero. The original WBA ruling established the timetable.

The cut over Lopez’s right eyebrow may delay the consolidation fight. November 19 is less than three months away, leaving limited time for the wound to heal before he resumes sparring and completes another camp. His team can request a medical extension if contact training places the cut at risk of reopening. Any added time would only postpone the obligation unless Catterall accepts a step-aside agreement or the WBA grants Lopez permission to take another fight. That delay may allow Lopez’s team to pursue Garcia, Benn or Haney.

Less money and greater risk make Catterall an opponent Teofimo has little reason to welcome. Based on Saturday’s performance, Lopez will need more than steady pressure and a busy jab against a disciplined southpaw who will make him pay for every mistake.

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Defeats Rolly Romero, Captures WBA Title
Sports.content:
That was Romero’s best stretch of the fight. Lopez recovered in the sixth and resumed moving forward behind his jab while attacking the body. Although the cut began bleeding again late in the contest, he continued outworking a champion who spent too much time waiting for isolated counterpunching opportunities.

Needing a strong finish, Romero remained cautious during the 12th. Lopez stayed on the front foot and completed the fight as the busier boxer. The victory raised his record to 23-2 with 13 knockouts, while Romero dropped to 17-3 with 13 stoppages.

Gary Antonio Russell Takes Santillan’s Interim Belt

A dominant unanimous decision over Victor Santillan gave Gary Antonio Russell the interim WBA super bantamweight title. Scores were 119-108 twice and 118-109.

Superior speed, a sharp jab and faster combinations allowed Russell to control the fight. The matchup between two southpaws produced frequent clinches, but Russell consistently landed the cleaner punches whenever space opened between them.

A right hook to the top of the head dropped Santillan during the 12th round. He beat referee Robert Hoyle’s count and held repeatedly to survive until the final bell. Russell moved to 22-1 with 13 knockouts, while Santillan fell to 16-3 with seven stoppages.

Hernandez Receives Majority Decision Over Veron

A majority decision over Francisco Daniel Veron gave Yoenli “El Diablo” Hernandez the victory in their 10-round middleweight bout. Two judges scored it widely for Hernandez at 99-91 and 98-92, while the third returned a surprising 95-95 card.

Heavier and more accurate punches gave Hernandez control during the opening rounds, while Veron tried to compensate with pressure and a high work rate. Veron created his best moment in the fifth when a check hook briefly wobbled Hernandez and forced him toward the ropes.

The Cuban regained control by attacking the body and landing right hands and uppercuts. Veron continued advancing and throwing through the final bell, but many of his punches missed or struck Hernandez’s guard.

Utria Edges Mercado By Split Decision

A disputed split decision over Israel “Bad Ways” Mercado kept Carlos Utria’s perfect record intact after their 10-round light welterweight fight. Scores were 96-94 for Utria, 96-94 for Mercado and 97-93 for Utria.

Much of the early action belonged to Utria before Mercado closed the fourth with a combination. The fight remained close through the middle rounds, with neither boxer establishing a lasting advantage.

Strong work during the ninth carried Mercado into a decisive final round. He believed he had done enough to win, and sections of the crowd expressed their displeasure when Utria was announced as the victor.

Marco Romero Stops Kahlil Mitchell In First

A sustained attack from Marco Romero forced a first-round stoppage against Kahlil “Killa” Mitchell in their scheduled eight-round bout.

Unable to defend himself, Mitchell was trapped as Romero unloaded a combination during the final minute. Referee Allen Huggins stopped the contest at 2:33.

Johnson Decisions Rodriguez

A six-round decision over Jose Gabriel Rodriguez gave Benjamin Johnson another welterweight victory. Johnson moved to 8-0 with seven knockouts, while Rodriguez dropped to 4-4-1.

Tony Weeks served as the referee.

Brown Sweeps Wiggins Over Six Rounds

Every round went to Joseph “The Prodigy” Brown in a slow six-round middleweight contest against Alton Wiggins. All three judges scored the fight 60-54.

Cleaner punches separated Brown from Wiggins, whose frequent holding prevented the exchanges from developing. The same pattern continued through the sixth.

Blancas Drops Mamone, Wins Decision

A knockdown helped Aldo Blancas secure a unanimous decision over Ricky Mamone in their four-round light welterweight bout. Scores were 39-36 twice and 40-35.

A left hook to the body from Blancas produced a delayed knockdown late in the second. Mamone beat referee John McCarthy’s count and continued despite bleeding from the nose during the third.

Unable to secure the stoppage, Blancas settled for the decision after Mamone survived the final round.

Jimmy Lennon Jr. served as the ring announcer.

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Wins Third Belt As Rolando Romero Barely Fights
Sports.content:
Romero’s strategy depended almost entirely on catching Lopez as he moved inside. That opportunity arrived in the fifth round when a left hand opened a cut over Lopez’s right eyebrow and hurt him. Romero followed with a flurry and had the challenger under pressure as “Rolly” chants spread through the arena.

It should have changed the fight. Instead, Romero returned to waiting.

Lopez recovered in the sixth, reestablished his jab and resumed attacking the body. Blood continued leaking from the cut during the later rounds, but it never prevented him from moving forward or maintaining his output. Romero landed isolated counters without putting enough punches behind them to take control.

The champion’s corner urged him to hold the center of the ring before the final round. He continued moving away and never produced the desperate attack required from a fighter in danger of losing his belt. By then, the crowd had grown restless after repeatedly waiting for Romero to open up.

Lopez deserves credit for remaining disciplined after being hurt. He avoided turning the fight into the reckless exchange Romero needed, kept scoring with straightforward work and closed the championship rounds on the front foot. The performance was controlled rather than destructive, with Lopez winning through activity, positioning and better decision-making.

His welterweight debut also raised a question about his punching power at 147 pounds. Lopez landed plenty of clean shots but never seriously hurt Romero. That may become important against the stronger and more active fighters in the division.

Still, Lopez accomplished what he came to Las Vegas to do. He won a title in a third weight class, while Romero surrendered his belt through passivity after finding the punch that briefly gave him a chance to take over the fight.

Sports.title: Yoenli Hernandez Beats Franciso Veron, But Draw Card Stuns
Sports.content:
Early confidence led the Cuban to lower his hands, pose and attack with wide power shots. He controlled the distance when he used his jab and footwork, then punished Veron with right hands, uppercuts and combinations to the body whenever the Argentine moved inside.

Veron’s persistence created one dangerous moment. A check hook late in the fifth round caught Hernandez cleanly, briefly wobbling him and forcing him toward the ropes. It was the clearest round for Veron and a reminder that Hernandez was taking unnecessary chances against an opponent who refused to retreat.

The favorite responded by tightening his defense and resuming his body attack. Hernandez hurt Veron with a right hand early in the eighth, followed with uppercuts and continued landing the stronger punches through the championship rounds. Veron absorbed the punishment and kept throwing, but his aggression rarely produced clean scoring shots.

That inability to secure the stoppage will give Hernandez something to study. He had the size, power and technical advantage, yet spent too much time looking for single explosive punches instead of breaking Veron down with sustained combinations. His performance was convincing without being the destructive statement his team likely wanted.

None of that explains the draw score. Hernandez clearly won more than five rounds, and the 95-95 card turned an otherwise straightforward result into an unnecessary controversy. The two wide scores properly reflected a fight controlled by Hernandez, even if Veron’s toughness forced him to work until the final bell.

Sports.title: Rolando Romero vs Teofimo Lopez Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 12

An unusual embrace opened the final round as the challenger whispered something to Romero before being pushed away. Lopez then resumed pressing forward and kept the champion from producing the desperate attack he needed.

Romero’s corner instructed him to hold the center of the ring, but he continued moving away and never forced a sustained exchange. Lopez closed the fight with greater activity and control, completing what should be a wide decision victory.

10-9 Lopez, 118-110 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 11

The challenger continued pressing behind his jab despite blood dripping from the cut over his right eye. Romero opened with a right to the body, added a shovel hook and later connected with another clean right hand.

Those isolated punches were not accompanied by enough urgency. Romero spent much of the round circling away before both fighters traded near the bell. Lopez’s higher output and forward pressure earned him another round, leaving the champion needing a knockout in the 12th.

10-9 Lopez, 108-101 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 10

Another slow round favored the challenger, who continued attacking the body and landed a clean right hand upstairs. He remained busier and controlled the range despite the cut over his right eye beginning to bleed again.

Romero increased his jab slightly but continued retreating and failed to apply the pressure needed to change the fight. The champion’s cautious approach cost him another round despite having much of the crowd behind him.

10-9 Lopez, 98-92 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 9

An early attempt by the champion to move forward produced little offense. Lopez quickly resumed control behind his jab, worked the body and maintained the distance while operating comfortably from the front foot.

Long stretches passed without a meaningful exchange as Romero kept his hands low and waited for counters that never developed. The earlier “Rolly” chants faded, and the crowd became restless with the champion’s passive approach.

10-9 Lopez, 88-83 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 8

Greater activity allowed the challenger to control another round. He moved forward behind combinations, landed clean hooks upstairs and blocked many of Romero’s counters before answering with punches of his own.

Romero continued picking isolated moments to exchange but remained too cautious to match Lopez’s output. The cut over Lopez’s right eye stayed under control as he extended his lead with cleaner and more consistent work.

10-9 Lopez, 78-74 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 7

Steady pressure from the challenger forced Romero to spend much of the round moving laterally and looking for counters. Both landed right hands early before Lopez attacked the body with a flurry. One punch strayed low and brought a warning from the referee.

Romero connected with a left hook at the bell that appeared to wobble Lopez. The late punch gave the champion another dangerous moment, but Lopez’s activity and control over most of the round narrowly earned it.

10-9 Lopez, 68-65 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 6

The challenger regained his composure after being hurt in the fifth and returned to applying pressure behind the jab. Working patiently from long range allowed him to control the distance and slow the pace.

Romero looked for counters but could not build on his success from the previous round. Lopez’s disciplined boxing and greater activity steadied the fight and secured the sixth.

10-9 Lopez, 58-56 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 5

The champion produced his strongest round yet, hurting Lopez with a left hand that opened a cut over his right eyebrow. Romero followed with a flurry and hurt him again with about a minute remaining.

Lopez answered late as the fighters exchanged punches and words, but Romero’s power and increased activity created the first major change in the fight. Chants of “Rolly” spread through T-Mobile Arena as the challenger finished the round under pressure.

10-9 Romero, 48-47 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 4

A stronger stand from the champion produced his best round of the fight. Several left hands connected cleanly, including one that briefly disrupted Lopez’s balance. The challenger continued pressing forward, but the sharper counters interrupted his rhythm and prevented him from controlling the exchanges.

Lopez’s activity kept the round competitive, although the more meaningful punches came from Romero.

10-9 Romero, 39-37 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 3

Teo continued moving forward, although Romero showed more willingness to hold his position and engage. Neither fighter landed a damaging punch as much of the action consisted of tentative jabs, feints and missed attempts from long range.

Romero remained focused on finding a counter, but Lopez’s greater activity and control of the distance narrowly gave him another quiet round.

10-9 Lopez, 30-27 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 2

Lopez continued setting the pace behind an active jab while forcing Romero to give ground. A clean right hand and several body shots helped Lopez establish his rhythm. Romero remained patient and looked for counters, including a check left hook, but spent too much of the round waiting for openings.

Both fighters missed during a wild exchange near the bell. Lopez’s higher output, effective jab and cleaner punches secured another round.

10-9 Lopez, 20-18 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 1

Both fighters opened cautiously at long range, using their jabs to measure distance without committing to extended combinations. Lopez applied more forward pressure and landed the cleaner jabs, while Romero remained patient and looked for counterpunching opportunities.

A counter right from Lopez connected late as Romero moved forward. Romero answered with a right hand before the bell, but Lopez’s greater activity and sharper work gave him the close opening round.

10-9 Lopez

Yoenli Hernandez defeats Francisco Veron

A surprisingly wide disagreement among the judges ended with Yoenli Hernandez defeating Francisco Daniel Veron by majority decision in their 10-round middleweight co-feature. Hernandez won by scores of 99-91 and 98-92, while the third judge produced a questionable 95-95 card.

Cleaner and heavier punches allowed Hernandez to control most of the fight. The Cuban attacked the body, landed sharp right hands and repeatedly caught Veron with uppercuts at close range. Veron pressed forward and maintained a high output, but many of his punches missed or struck Hernandez’s guard.

Veron created his best moment in the fifth when a check hook briefly wobbled Hernandez and forced him toward the ropes. Hernandez recovered and regained control, hurting Veron with a right hand early in the eighth before dominating the final two rounds.

The challenger’s chin carried him to the final bell despite absorbing numerous power punches. Hernandez never found the stoppage he wanted, but his accurate work made the 95-95 score difficult to explain.

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 9

Hernandez continued landing the cleaner punches, although some of his shots lacked full force. Veron walked directly into a right hand but absorbed it well and kept pressing forward. His toughness kept him in the fight, but he could not produce enough accurate offense to take the round.

10-9 Hernandez, 89-82 Hernandez

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 8

Hernandez hurt Veron with a right hand early in the round and moved in for the finish, but Veron avoided the follow-up attack. Hernandez returned to the body before landing a combination upstairs and two uppercuts that lifted Veron’s chin. Veron answered once again, although Hernandez’s cleaner and harder punches secured the round.

10-9 Hernandez, 79-73 Hernandez

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 7

Hernandez landed a right hand at close range before partially connecting with an uppercut and following with another right. The Cuban then increased his body attack and struck Veron with clubbing punches on the inside. Veron absorbed everything without going down, but Hernandez controlled another round with the heavier work.

10-9 Hernandez, 69-64 Hernandez

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 6

Hernandez connected with several chopping punches, but Veron continued answering with a high volume of shots. Most of Veron’s punches missed or struck the guard, while Hernandez landed the cleaner work during the exchanges. CompuBox credited Veron with only 24 connects from 171 punches across rounds five and six. Hernandez landed 42 of 128 during the same stretch.

10-9 Hernandez, 59-55 Hernandez

After Five Rounds: Hernandez Remains in Control

Hernandez has controlled most of the fight, but Veron’s check hook at the end of the fifth showed that he remains dangerous. Hernandez needs to continue attacking the body without becoming careless while pressing for a stoppage. A convincing victory would place him near a world-title opportunity, but getting reckless against Veron could undo an otherwise strong performance.

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 5

Hernandez landed a heavy right hand during the opening minute, but Veron absorbed it and immediately answered. Hernandez avoided the return before attacking the body and connecting with a right uppercut, a two-punch combination and a left hook. Just when Hernandez seemed to be taking full control, Veron caught him with a check hook that badly wobbled him and stole the round.

10-9 Veron, 49-46 Hernandez

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 4

An overhand right from Hernandez shook Veron at close range before a body shot and two more power punches disrupted his balance. Hernandez continued working downstairs and found the target with a left hook. Veron landed a late flurry, but Hernandez took the punches without showing any effect.

10-9 Hernandez, 40-36 Hernandez

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 3

Hernandez briefly lost his balance after taking a right hand, then answered with a long right and a hard one-two that forced Veron backward. Hernandez continued applying pressure, although many of his heavier punches struck Veron’s guard rather than landing cleanly. Veron’s responsible defense kept him competitive.

10-9 Hernandez, 30-27 Hernandez

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 2

Hernandez pushed Veron backward with power punches, but much of his work landed on the guard. An uppercut-left hook combination came close before Hernandez connected with a sharp right hook at close range. He continued closing the distance and controlling the exchanges.

10-9 Hernandez, 20-18 Hernandez

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 1

Hernandez attacked immediately, landing an overhand right that knocked Veron slightly off balance. A straight left split the guard before Hernandez went to the body and followed with punches upstairs. Veron answered with a double left at close range, but Hernandez’s right uppercut and cleaner power shots gave him the round.

10-9 Hernandez

Russell Dominates Santillan

Gary Antonio Russell captured the interim WBA super bantamweight title with a one-sided unanimous decision over Victor Santillan. The judges scored the 12-round bout 119-108, 119-108 and 118-109.

Russell (22-1, 13 KOs) controlled the distance with his faster hands, accurate jab and sharp combinations. Santillan (16-3, 7 KOs) struggled to deal with Russell’s movement and spent much of the fight being beaten to the punch. Russell completed the dominant performance by dropping Santillan during the final round and nearly forcing a stoppage before the bell.

Carlos Utria Edges Israel Mercado by Split Decision

A difficult U.S. debut ended with Carlos Utria narrowly defeating Israel Mercado by split decision after 10 competitive light welterweight rounds. Mercado disrupted the Colombian prospect’s rhythm, pressed forward and made the heavy favorite work harder than anticipated. Utria found success with body punches and short combinations, but he never gained complete control of the fight. Scores were 96-94 and 97-93 for Utria, while the third judge gave Mercado a 96-94 card.

Marco Romero Stops Kahlil Mitchell in First Round

A fast start allowed Marco Romero to overwhelm Kahlil Mitchell and force a stoppage at 2:33 of the opening round. The 20-year-old middleweight landed hard combinations almost immediately, giving Mitchell little time to settle into the fight. Referee intervention ended the scheduled eight-round bout before the first bell.

Benjamin Johnson Decisions Jose Gabriel Rodriguez

The opening fight of the evening ended with Benjamin Johnson earning a unanimous decision over Jose Gabriel Rodriguez after six welterweight rounds. Johnson used his 6-foot-2 frame and 76-inch reach to control the distance against the shorter Ecuadorian. Rodriguez remained durable and became the first opponent to take the 21-year-old prospect to the final bell. Johnson had stopped each of his first seven opponents before Saturday night.

Joseph Brown Sweeps Alton Wiggins

A six-round shutout gave Joseph Brown a unanimous decision over Alton Wiggins in their junior middleweight bout. The 19-year-old controlled the distance with his height and reach, winning each round without scoring a knockdown. All three judges returned scores of 60-54.

Aldo Blancas Decisions Ricky Mamone

Aldo Blancas used his height, reach and strong left hand to defeat Ricky Mamone by unanimous decision in a four-round light welterweight bout. Blancas dropped Mamone with a left to the body in the second round and controlled most of the action from distance. Mamone recovered and made it to the final bell, but he could not overcome the early knockdown or Blancas’ higher output. The judges scored it 39-36, 39-36 and 40-35.

Sports.title: Marco Romero Destroys Kahlil Mitchell in First Round
Sports.content:
Mitchell never had an opportunity to settle into the scheduled eight-round fight. Romero closed the distance quickly, landed clean punches and continued firing combinations once he had his opponent near the ropes. The pressure became too much for Mitchell before the first round ended.

“I’m not getting paid for overtime,” Romero said after the fight.

That line matched the performance. Romero did not rush forward, throwing wild punches in search of an early finish. His shots were short and accurate, and he remained balanced while attacking. Those qualities separate him from young punchers who rely almost entirely on physical strength.

Although Mitchell was not a major test, Romero handled him exactly as a highly regarded prospect should. There was no prolonged feeling-out period and no opportunity for the underdog to gain confidence.

Romero (15-0, 13 KOs) recently signed with Premier Boxing Champions, giving the company another young middleweight with the potential to move quickly. His power will attract attention, but his composure is just as important. He fights like someone who already understands how to create openings rather than waiting for an opponent to make an obvious mistake.

Stronger opposition will be needed before Romero can be judged against the leading fighters at 160 pounds. Saturday’s performance still provided an impressive introduction for viewers watching him for the first time.

Mitchell came to Las Vegas with six professional wins and four knockouts. Romero made that experience look insignificant, finishing him before the fight had a chance to develop.

Sports.title: George Liddard Stops Dario Morello After Eight Rounds
Sports.content:
The 24-year-old Liddard moved to 15-0 with nine knockouts after adding the European championship to the British, Commonwealth, and IBF Intercontinental belts he previously held.

Morello struggled to land consistently against the quicker champion. Many of his wider punches missed, allowing Liddard to score with straighter combinations before moving out of range. The Italian never found a way to slow him down and lost each completed round.

Officials recorded a retirement after eight rounds. Morello fell to 26-2 with four knockouts.

Jimmy Sains Defeats Tom Cowling

Jimmy Sains claimed the vacant Commonwealth middleweight title with a 12-round unanimous decision over Tom Cowling.

Much of the opening half belonged to Sains, although Cowling landed a solid right hand late in the first round and enjoyed his best stretch during rounds six and seven. A sustained attack in the sixth briefly forced Sains onto the defensive.

The southpaw regained command from the eighth and swept most of the remaining rounds with his higher output. Cowling rocked him with another right hand during the final minute, but the late success was not enough to change the outcome.

The judges scored the contest 119-109, 119-109, and 118-110 for Sains, who raised his record to 13-0 with 10 knockouts. Cowling dropped to 15-2.

Buttigieg And Gordon Fight To Split Draw

Emmanuel Buttigieg and P A Gordon fought to a 10-round split draw, leaving the vacant English middleweight title unclaimed.

Gordon had the stronger start and held the advantage through much of the opening four rounds. Buttigieg increased his output in the fifth and sixth before Gordon answered during a series of closely contested later rounds.

Both men fought aggressively in the tenth with the decision still unsettled. Gordon bloodied Buttigieg’s nose during an entertaining finish, but the judges were unable to agree on a winner.

One card favored Gordon 97-93, another had Buttigieg ahead 96-94, and the third was level at 95-95. Buttigieg is now 12-0-1, while Gordon moved to 9-0-1.

Tiah Mai Ayton Stops Ellie Hellewell

Tiah Mai Ayton won the vacant Commonwealth featherweight title when Ellie Hellewell retired after the sixth round.

A combination near the end of the opening round began creating separation for Ayton. She continued landing the cleaner punches over the following rounds and hurt Hellewell again late in the fifth.

Hellewell completed the sixth, but her corner ended the contest before round seven. Officials recorded a sixth-round retirement, advancing Ayton to 7-0 with six knockouts.

Copper Box Undercard Results

Connor Mitchell defeated Caine Singh on points over four rounds in a featherweight bout. A left hand from Mitchell dropped Singh in the opening round, and referee Lewis Van Poetsch scored the contest 39-37. The victory moved Mitchell to 4-0 with two knockouts.

Louie Ward knocked out Jon Martinez at 2:36 of the third round. A right-left combination sent Martinez down for the full count.

Ioan Croft stopped Tomas Andres Reynoso at 1:50 of the sixth round. A left hand dropped Reynoso in the second before another sustained attack forced the stoppage four rounds later.

Harley Burrows needed only 65 seconds to stop Carlos Miguel Ronner. A series of unanswered punches led referee Kieran McCann to end the middleweight contest.

The official results are confirmed by the British Boxing Board of Control.

Ghana News.title: I haven’t experienced any envy in the gospel music industry — Ohemaa Mercy
Ghana News.content:
Gospel musician Ohemaa Mercy, born Mercy Twum-Ampofo, says she has not experienced envy within the gospel music industry, dismissing suggestions that the sector is characterised by jealousy and rivalry.

She said although envy and malice could exist in any industry that attracted public attention, she could not speak authoritatively about such sentiments among gospel musicians because she had not personally encountered them.

Speaking on Prime Time with George and Mercury Quaye on August 19, 2026, the 'Oheneba' hitmaker said she remained focused on her calling and had not allowed herself to be distracted by perceptions of envy within the industry.

“The devil is everywhere, but I have not heard of any envy in the gospel music industry. I’ve not experienced it, so I can’t talk about it,” Ohemaa Mercy said.

She said she remained confident in her calling and believed that her faith and divine backing would enable her to overcome any opposition she might encounter.

“No one can stop me, because I’m not alone. The host of heaven is with me,” she stated.

Tehillah Experience

Ohemaa Mercy also spoke about the spiritual significance of her annual Tehillah Experience, which is now in its 13th year.

She described the event as a revival that reaches families and challenges what she described as spiritual strongholds, saying its impact had attracted opposition from the devil.

“Spiritually, there’s a battle by the devil himself because Tehillah Experience breaks into families’ altars. It’s basically a revival, and it comes like a burning fire,” she said.

She attributed the continued success of the event to prayer and God's intervention.

“God is helping me because of my prayers,” she added.

The gospel musician explained that because the Tehillah Experience was organised as a free event, she had to make personal sacrifices to finance and sustain it.

She disclosed that on some occasions, she had sold her cars to raise funds to keep the event going.

“Sometimes I have to sell some of my cars to make sure that Tehillah Experience moves on. I sell my car and walk, because without sacrifice, you cannot see the glory,” she said.

Music and spirituality

Ohemaa Mercy further disclosed that she never released a song without first praying over it, stressing that she believed God's hand should accompany her music.

She cited her song 'Mennwu Da' as an example, saying she believed its message could have a profound impact on listeners, including patients in hospitals.

According to her, gospel music should not be treated as ordinary entertainment because of its potential spiritual impact.

“You cannot release a song just like that. Even worldly musicians seek God,” she said.

Ohemaa Mercy's comments reflect her conviction that her music and the Tehillah Experience are extensions of her Christian faith and ministry, rather than merely artistic or entertainment ventures.

Ghana News.title: Prayer does not solve everything — Ohemaa Mercy
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian gospel musician Ohemaa Mercy has urged Christians to complement prayer with hard work and practical action, saying prayer alone cannot solve every problem.

According to the award-winning artiste, some challenges require practical solutions rather than a purely spiritual approach.

Speaking on Prime Time with George and Mercury Quaye on August 19, 2026, Ohemaa Mercy said Christians should learn to distinguish between issues that require prayer and those that demand personal effort and responsibility.

“Do you know prayer doesn’t solve everything? Some things are not spiritual; you just have to get the right channel to work with,” she said.

She explained that while prayer was important, individuals must also take responsibility for their actions and work towards achieving their goals.

“You don’t have to disturb God over everything. If I want to pass my exams, I have to learn. If I don’t learn and I go to the exam hall, and I’m sitting there praying, how will I pass the exams?” she asked.

The gospel musician also cautioned Christians against relying solely on prayer when they could take practical steps to improve their financial circumstances.

“If I need money, how will I get the money? I need to work. I can’t sit there for money to fall like manna,” she said.

Ohemaa Mercy particularly encouraged unemployed young people to identify their talents, explore available opportunities and take advantage of technology while continuing to pray for greater opportunities.

“There are some things prayer doesn’t solve. You have to write applications, and even if you are not getting office work, there is some potential in you. You need to start something. Now the internet is open, and there’s a lot you can do to get money,” she said.

She encouraged young people not to despise humble beginnings, stressing that they could start small while trusting God for bigger opportunities.

“You can start from somewhere whilst you are praying, and God can open big doors for you,” she added.

The gospel musician further called on Christians to strike a balance between their religious commitments and their professional responsibilities.

She advised churchgoers to remain committed to their faith without allowing church activities to interfere with working hours or their ability to earn a living.

Ohemaa Mercy also urged parents to develop close and open relationships with their children to enable them to discuss sensitive issues, particularly as they grow into adolescence.

She cautioned parents against being overly strict or presenting themselves as too holy or unapproachable, saying this could prevent children from seeking guidance from them.

“When children are growing, that kind of feeling comes. So you need to be like a friend to them to be able to draw them closer to guide them through that stage,” she said.

She explained that children needed parents who could listen to them and provide guidance as they navigated the emotional and social challenges that come with growing up.

“If you are too ‘Holyghostic’ and your children cannot vibe with you, you’ll lose them. And what they can’t get from their mother or father, they will get it out there,” she added.

Ohemaa Mercy's comments highlight the need for Christians to combine faith with personal responsibility, practical action and open communication within the family.

Ghana News.title: New PURC office symbolises stronger consumer protection – Dr Jinapor
Ghana News.content:
Dr John Abdulai Jinapor, Minister of Energy and Green Transition, says the new head office of the Public Utilities Regulatory Commission (PURC) symbolises stronger utility regulation and consumer protection.

‎He said the facility should enable the PURC to deepen regulatory oversight, improve consumer services and ensure that utility companies remain financially viable to provide reliable services.

‎Dr Jinapor said this when he commissioned the new PURC head office complex in Accra, describing it as a “fitting home” for an institution of national importance.

‎He said the PURC had evolved over more than two and a half decades from an institution largely associated with tariff reviews into a regulator with broader responsibilities for the electricity, water and natural gas sectors.

‎The Minister said the Commission’s mandate extended beyond consumer protection to ensure utility companies operated sustainably and met their financial and operational obligations.

‎He urged the PURC to strengthen enforcement, intensify scrutiny of the commercial performance of utilities and ensure that consumers felt the presence of the regulator through improved service delivery and faster resolution of complaints.

‎“Sometimes, once you strengthen enforcement, you step on toes, but you have to step on toes sometimes to ensure that you achieve your objective,” he said.

‎Dr Jinapor particularly urged the Commission to pay close attention to the commercial performance of the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG), describing it as a critical link in the financial sustainability of the energy sector.

‎He also encouraged the PURC to broaden stakeholder engagement and support industrial competitiveness, particularly in relation to the Government’s 24-hour economy agenda.

‎Dr Shafic Suleman, Executive Secretary of the PURC, said the new head office represented a significant investment in the future of utility regulation in Ghana and reflected the Commission’s institutional growth.

‎He said the facility had been designed with modern systems and facilities to respond to the increasing complexities of utility regulation.

‎The complex includes modern conference spaces for stakeholder engagement, state-of-the-art training facilities, electricity and water meter laboratories for quality assurance, a real-time monitoring room and contemporary offices to improve operational efficiency.

‎Dr Suleman expressed appreciation to successive boards, management and staff, the Government and other stakeholders for their contributions towards completing the project.

‎He said the building was fully paid for through improved cash flows within the utility sector, attributing the development partly to reforms that had strengthened the Cash Waterfall Mechanism.

‎Mr Moses Asaga, PURC Board Chairman, described the new facility as a testament to the growth and enduring mandate of the Commission to protect consumers while ensuring that utilities remained financially viable.

‎He recalled that when the PURC was established in 1997, it operated from a colonial-era building with about 12 management and staff.

‎Mr Asaga said the new facility represented a remarkable transformation of the Commission and challenged management and staff to steward it with diligence while delivering higher standards of service to the people of Ghana.

‎He reaffirmed the Board’s commitment to working with the Presidency and the Ministry of Energy and Green Transition to strengthen regulation and advance a well-functioning utility sector.

‎The new head office is expected to provide an improved working environment for staff and strengthen the PURC’s capacity to regulate Ghana’s electricity, water and natural gas utilities.

Ghana News.title: Rev. Wengam re-elected Assemblies of God, Ghana General Superintendent
Ghana News.content:
Rev. Stephen Yenusom Wengam has been overwhelmingly re-elected as General Superintendent of Assemblies of God, Ghana, securing nearly 90 per cent of votes cast during the church’s 32nd Biennial General Council Meeting at Gomoa Fetteh in the Central Region.

Rev. Wengam, who also serves as Head Pastor of Cedar Mountain Chapel at East Legon, polled 3,727 votes, representing 89.61 per cent, to defeat Rev. Dr. Kwame B. Bansah of Charity Assemblies of God in the Adenta District of the Accra West Region, who obtained 432 votes, representing 10.39 per cent.

The election returned Rev. Wengam to office for another four-year term and completed the process of electing the church’s top leadership team.

A total of 4,159 valid votes were cast in the contest for General Superintendent, while seven ballots were rejected, bringing the total votes cast to 4,166.

Rev. Dr. Kwadwo Bempah of Holy Hill Chapel in the Adabraka District of the Accra West Region was elected Assistant General Superintendent, while Rev. Dr. Albert Anane of The Father’s House in Koforidua, Eastern Region “A”, emerged as the new General Secretary.

Rev. Simon Abu Baba of Central Chapel in Mim retained his position as General Treasurer after standing unopposed.

In the departmental elections, Rev. Mrs Esther Oduro Dwomo was elected National Women’s Ministries Director, while Mr. Silas Amankwaah retained his position as National Men’s Ministry Director unopposed.

Rev. Michael K. N. Atisu and Rev. Henry Kyei Mensah also retained their positions unopposed as National Sunday School Ministry Director and National Youth Ministries Director respectively.

The meeting also saw the appointment of new officers, with Rev. Boniface Keelson named Foreign Missions Director and Rev. Aaron Lambon Fant, adjudged Best Church Planter at the event, appointed Home Missions Director.

Delivering his acceptance speech, Rev. Wengam pledged to serve members of the church with renewed commitment, humility and dedication.

“To all who endorsed me with your precious votes, you will never regret your sacred decision,” he said.

He described the electoral process as peaceful, fair and transparent, noting that despite the competitive nature of elections, the exercise was characterised by minimal acrimony.

Rev. Wengam called on members to move beyond the contest and unite behind the church’s mission.

“After competition comes cooperation. The competition for the highest position in Assemblies of God, Ghana, is over. A gigantic task to build the church remains,” he said.

Using a local proverb to underscore the importance of unity, he noted that “one person cannot embrace a baobab tree,” stressing that the responsibility of building the church required the collective efforts of leaders and members at all levels.

The General Superintendent said his second term would focus on advancing the church’s transformation agenda and ensuring the successful implementation of its strategic initiatives.

Among the key projects he highlighted was the Centenary City Project, which is being undertaken to commemorate the church’s 100th anniversary.

“The Centenary City Project to mark our 100 years will certainly materialise in our lifetime,” he stated

He also reaffirmed the church’s commitment to evangelism under the MM33 agenda of the World Assemblies of God Fellowship.

“We are determined to evangelise the entire nation and reach every village, every town and every city with the Gospel,” he said.

Rev. Wengam expressed confidence that the church would continue to grow by harnessing the talents and expertise of its members.

“Leadership is about turning bold ideas into shared progress,” he added.

Reflecting on his landslide victory, Rev. Wengam observed that his support had risen significantly since his first election four years ago.

“Four years ago, you gave me 61 per cent. Four years later, you gave me almost 90 per cent,” he said.

He thanked both supporters and those who voted for his opponent, describing all participants as important contributors to the church’s democratic process.

Rev. Wengam also appealed for reconciliation after the elections and encouraged unsuccessful candidates not to lose hope.

Recalling his defeat in a regional secretary election in 2014, he said setbacks could sometimes be part of God’s preparation for greater responsibilities.

“You don’t need to be an Executive Presbytery member. You don’t need to be a district pastor. God can catapult you from anywhere once you remain faithful and committed,” he said.

Looking ahead, the General Superintendent announced that the church’s attention would now shift to the World Assemblies of God Fellowship Congress, scheduled to take place in Ghana from October 14 to 16, 2026.

He noted that the congress would be the first such global gathering to be hosted in Africa and urged pastors and church members across the country to support and participate in the event, particularly the evening sessions expected to be held at the Accra Sports Stadium.

“Hosting an event of global significance comes with enormous responsibilities,” he said.

Following the declaration of results and announcement of appointments, Rev. Gregg T. Johnson, the main speaker for the council meeting, delivered a sermon urging pastors to keep God’s fire burning, describing it as a symbol of God’s presence.

Rev. Wengam later led prayers for spiritual renewal, church growth and God’s glory to be manifested among members.

He also prayed for the sick and both outgoing and newly elected Executive Presbytery officers, assisted by Rev. Dr. Bempah.

The peaceful conclusion of the elections and the 32nd Biennial General Council Meeting, the church’s highest decision-making body, paves the way for the newly elected Executive Presbytery to lead Assemblies of God, Ghana, over the next four years.

Ghana News.title: Less than 20km of clearing left to connect Accra-Kumasi Expressway to Kumasi – Agbodza
Ghana News.content:
Roads Minister, Kwame Agbodza

The Minister for Roads and Highways, Governs Kwame Agbodza, says less than 20 kilometres of clearing work remains on the Accra-Kumasi Expressway before the project reaches Kumasi.

Mr Agbodza said the project had made significant progress and was now only a short stretch away from connecting with the Kumasi Orbiter, also known as the Kumasi Ring Road.

“We have less than 20 kilometres. I’m sure we have maybe around 10, 15 kilometres to hit Kumasi itself,” he said on Friday, August 21, 2026.

The Minister said the progress would pave the way for the expressway to connect with key road infrastructure around Kumasi.

Contractor back on site

Mr Agbodza also announced that Kofi Job Construction Limited had returned to site and was making progress on the project.

“Since then, the contractor, Kofi Job, has returned to site and is doing very well,” he said.

He explained that the contractor was nearing completion of one section of the road before moving to the other side, expressing confidence that the remaining works would be completed.

Asantehene’s support

Mr Agbodza acknowledged the support and guidance of the Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, on road infrastructure development in the Kumasi enclave.

He said the Asantehene had previously stressed the need to complete roads around the area to facilitate the operationalisation of the Sewua Hospital, which is expected to serve as a regional hospital for Kumasi.

The Minister also expressed appreciation to the Ghana Armed Forces for their support during the clearing exercise and thanked the Asantehene for his continued counsel and support for road development in the Ashanti Region.

Ghana News.title: US judge strikes down policy suspending immigrant visa processing for 75 nations
Ghana News.content:
A U.S. judge on Friday struck down, opens new tab a Trump administration policy suspending the issuance of immigrant visas to ​applicants from 75 countries, saying that the policy exceeded Secretary of ‌State Marco Rubio's statutory authority.

U.S. District Judge Jeannette Vargas in Manhattan said the policy that the State Department announced in January was "patently unlawful" and ran afoul of federal ​immigration law, which explicitly stripped the Secretary of State of ​authority over consular officers' processing of immigrant visas.

"The Policy, which categorically ⁠prohibits the issuance of immigrant visas based upon the nationality of ​the applicant, represents a direct abrogation of this statutory scheme," she wrote.

The State ​Department's suspension, which also took effect in January, impacted applicants from Latin American countries including Brazil, Colombia, and Uruguay; Balkan nations such as Bosnia and Albania; South Asian ​countries Pakistan and Bangladesh; and those from many nations in Africa, the ​Middle East, and the Caribbean.

The State Department said applicants from those countries were "at a ‌high ⁠risk for becoming a public charge and recourse to local, state and federal government resources in the United States." The department did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the ruling.

Vargas, an appointee of Democratic ​former President Joe ​Biden, issued the ⁠ruling in a lawsuit filed by immigrant rights groups Catholic Legal Immigration Network and African Communities Together along with ​applicants for immigrant visas and U.S. citizens who are ​sponsoring family ⁠members from the designated countries for immigrant visas.

President Donald Trump has pursued an aggressive immigration crackdown that he says is aimed at improving domestic security.

Rights groups ⁠say ​the crackdown has violated free speech and due ​process rights and has created an unsafe environment, particularly for ethnic minorities, who have raised ​concerns about racial profiling.

Ghana News.title: MCEs collecting fees from galamseyers are facilitating illegality – Ken Ashigbey
Ghana News.content:
Convener of the Media Coalition Against Galamsey, Ing. Ken Ashigbey, has accused some Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs) of facilitating illegal mining by collecting fees and charges from operators engaged in galamsey.

Ing. Ashigbey said the alleged practice raises serious questions about the commitment of local authorities to the fight against illegal mining, particularly when public institutions mandated to protect communities and the environment are accused of collecting revenue from activities deemed unlawful.

He argued that officials who knowingly facilitate illegal mining could potentially be held liable under Ghana's mining laws, which criminalise not only unauthorised mining but also acts that aid, facilitate, encourage or promote activities carried out in contravention of the law.

His comments come against the backdrop of the JoyNews investigative documentary, A Tax for Galamsey: The Extortion Racket Fuelling Illegal Mining, which exposed allegations that a district assembly in the Amansie Central District of the Ashanti Region had been collecting payments from operators of prohibited mining equipment.

The JoyNews investigation found alleged instances in which illegal miners were required to pay fees to enable them to continue operating, with payments reportedly formalised through stickers, receipts and other documentation linked to the District Assembly. The investigation described the arrangement as creating a parallel taxation system around illegal mining.

The exposé further reported that operators of changfan machines were allegedly charged about GH¢6,000 annually, while operators using excavators were also allegedly subjected to payments in exchange for continued operation.

The revelations triggered calls for investigations, with the government subsequently directing the relevant authorities to examine the allegations. The Lands Ministry said it had taken notice of the documentary and would investigate the conduct of officials implicated in the report.

Speaking on TV3 on Saturday, August 22, Ing. Ashigbey said investigations had uncovered instances in which officials of some assemblies allegedly went to illegal mining sites to collect fees and charges from operators.

He also alleged that some assemblies had charged miners for the use of equipment that the government had prohibited as part of efforts to combat galamsey.

“Then you also have the situation where these assemblies too would then take changfans, equipment that are proscribed by the government, which we say is illegal, and they charge for it; there is evidence; that evidence is collected by a media house, presented to the government, and what we hear is that it is not true,” he said.

The allegations are particularly significant in light of the Minerals and Mining (Amendment) Act, 2019 (Act 995), which amended the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703) to strengthen penalties for illegal mining and related offences.

The amended Section 99 criminalises conduct in which a person purposely aids, facilitates, encourages or promotes acts carried out in contravention of the mining law.

It also specifically criminalises the use of floating platforms and other equipment for mining in or along natural water bodies, as well as the provision of excavators or other equipment for mining operations contrary to the law.

The Minerals Commission lists Act 995 among the principal laws governing Ghana's mining sector, alongside the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703) and the 2015 amendment, Act 900.

Ing. Ashigbey therefore questioned why no decisive action had been taken against municipal and district authorities allegedly involved in collecting money from operators engaged in unlawful mining.

He challenged the argument that the issuance of receipts or the collection of officially sanctioned fees could legitimise an otherwise illegal activity.

“How is it that the MP for Oda mentions the DCE for Oda as charging 14,000 for people who are involved in illegality, and the MCE’s only defence is that they did not have a permit?” he asked.

Ing. Ashigbey further questioned whether the affected miners had obtained the necessary environmental permits before commencing their operations, insisting that the absence of the required authorisations would render the activities illegal.

His concerns echo the central finding of the JoyNews A Tax for Galamsey investigation: that the collection of fees from illegal mining operators risks creating the impression that payment to a public authority can substitute for the licences and environmental approvals required by law.

The issue has since moved beyond the initial Amansie Central allegations.

President John Dramani Mahama, speaking in March 2026, said the JoyNews exposé had helped uncover a practice that was not confined to one district. He said investigations indicated that several districts in gold-mining areas were engaging in similar revenue-collection practices involving mining equipment.

The President subsequently directed that assemblies should stop taxing changfan machines and other equipment associated with illegal mining, stressing that internally generated revenue should not be derived from unlawful activities. Government also warned MMDCEs to immediately stop taxing illegal miners and cautioned that officials who failed to comply could face sanctions.

The government position underscores the significance of Ing. Ashigbey's concerns over the role of local authorities in the galamsey fight.

He said authorities must confront the issue more decisively, warning that continued involvement of public officials in activities linked to illegal mining was deepening the environmental and economic consequences of galamsey.

“We don’t seem to see the challenge that is confronting us; this thing is eating us up,” he said.

The controversy also raises a broader question about the effectiveness of Ghana's decentralised system in the fight against illegal mining.

While MMDAs have responsibilities for local development and revenue mobilisation, Ing. Ashigbey's argument is that such responsibilities cannot extend to collecting revenue from activities that the state itself has declared illegal.

The JoyNews investigation has consequently placed the spotlight on whether local government structures are strengthening enforcement or, in some instances, creating financial incentives that allow illegal mining to continue.

Ghana News.title: Developer LMI Holdings commits to completing first 700 Saglemi housing units
Ghana News.content:
Developer LMI Holdings has committed to completing the first 700 housing units under the revived Saglemi Housing Project by March 2027, with the first phase of 1,500 units expected to be completed by December 2027.

A statement issued by the Presidency said the commitment was highlighted during President John Dramani Mahama’s inspection of the Saglemi project in the Greater Accra Region on Thursday, August 20.

The Saglemi project, originally conceived as a 5,000-unit affordable housing estate under the late President John Evans Atta Mills, stalled after a change in government, with subsequent legal and investigative processes bringing construction to a halt.

The prolonged inactivity also left the site vulnerable to vandalism, with electrical cables, fittings, wash basins, bathtubs, bulbs, and underground telecommunications cables reportedly removed.

President Mahama said the Government eventually decided to partner with the private sector to complete the development, leading to the selection of LMI Holdings to undertake the redevelopment.

“From what you have seen today, this estate is going to become a modern and conducive residential community for thousands of Ghanaian families,” President Mahama said.

He urged prospective homeowners to register promptly once the sales portal is opened, warning that demand for the houses is likely to be high.

“I want to encourage Ghanaians to register as soon as the sales portal is opened because these houses will be in high demand,” he said.

President Mahama explained that industries located along the corridor, particularly around Tema and the Dawa Industrial Park, could also seek to acquire the houses for their workers.

He said the estate would serve both industrial workers and Ghanaian families seeking to own homes in a well-planned community.

Beyond the housing development, President Mahama said Saglemi would benefit from major supporting infrastructure, including improved road and railway connections.

“Government is dualising the road from here to Aflao. The first phase is already under construction, while the second phase from Central University is being awarded. Residents will therefore enjoy a fast and efficient road connection,” he said.

He added that a planned railway connection would transport both passengers and cargo, including containers and industrial goods from the Tema Port to the industrial park.

According to President Mahama, these developments are positioning Saglemi as part of a major industrial and residential growth corridor and fit into government’s wider vision for a Green Digital City.

The President said he expected the developer to fulfil its commitment on the housing delivery timeline.

“It is my hope that shortly after Christmas, around Easter next year, we shall gather here to commission the first 700 housing units and hand them over to homeowners. Then, in December next year, we shall return once again to commission the remaining units, completing the first phase of 1,500 houses,” he said.

The first phase represents 1,500 units of the original 5,000-unit Saglemi project, with President Mahama indicating that work would subsequently commence on the remaining 3,500 units.

He also linked the project to government’s broader efforts to increase the supply of affordable housing and reduce the burden of high rent advances on Ghanaian families.

“Saglemi is not the last housing project. The government is preparing a major national housing programme that will be announced by the Finance Minister in the next budget,” he said.

President Mahama noted that GH¢500 million had already been allocated to the District Housing Scheme, with construction expected to begin in selected districts as government rolls out its housing agenda over the next four years.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
